title: fix: treat {% set x %}...{% endset %} block assignments as template-assigned variables
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13730

### Proposed Changes:

`_collect_assigned_variables` (`haystack/utils/jinja2_extensions.py`) collected only `nodes.Assign`, so a variable assigned with a block assignment, `{% set x %}...{% endset %}` (`nodes.AssignBlock`), inside an `if`/`for` block was inferred as an input variable. With the default `required_variables="*"`, `PromptBuilder` and `ChatPromptBuilder` failed with "Missing required input variables". `OutputAdapter` and `ConditionalRouter` got a mandatory input that a pipeline never connects. The same template written with `{% set x = ... %}` already worked since #10093 (for #9916).

The helper now collects both `Assign` and `AssignBlock` nodes. Both have a `target`, so the existing name/list/tuple handling applies unchanged. I used an annotated list instead of `find_all((Assign, AssignBlock))`, because the tuple form types the nodes as `Stmt` and mypy then rejects `.target`.

### How did you test it?

- New unit test `TestPromptBuilder::test_variables_correct_with_block_assignment`, next to the existing assignment/tuple/list-assignment tests. It fails on `main` (`variables == ['existing_documents', 'x']`) and passes with this change.
- `test/components/builders`, `test/components/converters/test_output_adapter.py`, `test/components/routers/test_conditional_router.py`, `test/utils/test_jinja2_extensions.py`: 242 passed.
- `ruff check`, `ruff format --check` and `mypy haystack/utils/jinja2_extensions.py` pass.
- Manually: the reproduction from #13730 renders with `PromptBuilder`, and `OutputAdapter`/`ConditionalRouter` inputs drop the spurious `x`.

### Notes for the reviewer

Release note: `releasenotes/notes/jinja2-block-set-variables-c52e62785ee67a1f.yaml`. I used Claude Code to prepare this change and reviewed and tested it myself.

title: feat: record the outputs_to_string tool result on the Agent tool span
body:
### Related Issues

- @ju-gu found the tool span confusing because it showed the raw tool output but not the `outputs_to_string` result the LLM actually received.

### Proposed Changes:

- The `haystack.agent.step.tool` span gets a new `haystack.agent.step.tool.result` content tag with the result string sent to the LLM. `haystack.agent.step.tool.output` still holds the raw tool return value.
- The tool-result message is now built inside the tool span (in the sync and async invoke closures). The State merge stays on the main thread in call order.
- The new tag follows the OTel GenAI `gen_ai.tool.call.result` concept on the `execute_tool` span.

### How did you test it?

Updated the tool span tag test and added sync/async tests with an `outputs_to_string` handler.

### Notes for the reviewer

- Langfuse only surfaces `*.input`/`*.output` tags, so showing the new tag there needs a follow-up in core-integrations (Rhesis likewise).
- If an output handler raises with `raise_on_failure=True`, the error is now raised inside the tool span. The failing call's `outputs_to_state` merge no longer runs before the raise.

title: fix: end the stream when a handle is closed before the producer starts
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13700

### Proposed Changes:

A task cancelled before its first step never runs any of the coroutine, so the `finally` in `runner()` that puts `_END_OF_STREAM` on the queue never executes. `aclose()` returns, `result` reports the cancellation, and a reader on the same handle stays in `await queue.get()` forever.

The marker is now also sent from the task's cancellation, via a done callback that only acts when the task was cancelled - a normal finish still sends it once, from the runner.

While doing that I also made `__aiter__` return instead of re-raising when the pipeline task was cancelled. It awaits the task on the marker so exceptions surface, and awaiting a cancelled task raises `CancelledError` in the reader; the reader has nothing left to do at that point, and `result` already reports the cancellation as a `RuntimeError`.

### How did you test it?

New test in `test/core/pipeline/test_async_pipeline_stream.py`: `stream()`, `aclose()` right after with no await in between, then collect from the handle under a 1s timeout. On the previous code it times out.

```
test/core/pipeline/test_async_pipeline_stream.py        21 passed
test/core/pipeline (excluding features/)               497 passed, 4 skipped
test/utils/test_async_utils.py test/components/agents   368 passed, 4 skipped
```

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean on both files.

---

This change was put together with an AI assistant. I traced the cancellation path in `runner()` / `aclose()`, reproduced the hang before touching anything, and ran the suites listed above on this branch.

### Notes for the reviewer

- The callback only fires on cancellation, so the existing "runner finished normally" path is untouched and the marker is not queued twice.
- `queue.put_nowait` is used in the callback since a done callback can't await; the queue is unbounded, so the `QueueFull` suppression should never trigger in practice.

title: fix: restore exact in-memory document store snapshots
body:
### Related Issues

No existing issue found for this snapshot-restoration path.

### Proposed Changes:

`InMemoryDocumentStore.load_from_disk()` used `OVERWRITE` when reconnecting to a saved shared index. Existing IDs were restored, but documents added after the snapshot remained searchable, including when loading an empty snapshot. BM25 statistics could therefore describe a mixture of saved and later data.

Reconstruct the saved documents before touching the index, then clear and rebuild documents and BM25 statistics under the existing per-index lock. Preserve the saved index identity and sharing configuration. With `shared=True`, other instances using that index observe the restored snapshot. The docstring states this shared-store effect, and the release note records a fix to undocumented merging behavior.

The restoration regression uses `shared=True` explicitly and only parameterizes empty/non-empty snapshots. The invalid-document preservation test also specifies `shared=True`. Short inline comments explain why documents are parsed before index mutation and why restoration holds the index lock.

### How did you test it?

The two narrowed shared-store regressions fail against the original production source at `bbe4efe50c716d6d05a0637980db3b641236e613`; the invalid-document preservation control passes. With the fix, all 7 load-from-disk cases pass, including four existing save/load tests covering binary blobs and sparse embeddings.

Checks on final commit `ad8f65c7fa7826707d6664041d6c5326ddb4f236`, Python 3.12.14 and Hatch 1.18.2:

title: fix(agent): don't seed State with None for omitted pipeline inputs
body:
Fixes #13680

## Problem

The same Agent with the same tool behaves differently by invocation path:

```
Agent alone      : top_k=5
Agent in pipeline: top_k=None
```

When the Agent runs inside a Pipeline and an input for a state-schema key is not provided, the Pipeline hands down `None` and the Agent seeds `State` with it - so a tool using `inputs_from_state` receives an explicit `None` instead of keeping its own default. Called directly, the key is absent from `kwargs` and the tool default survives.

Reproduced on `main` (d768bb8) with the issue's script.

## Fix

The approach proposed in the issue: skip `None` values when seeding State, so an input that was never provided does not become a state value.

Trade-off (as noted in the issue): at the Pipeline boundary an explicitly-passed `None` is indistinguishable from an omitted input, so both fall back to the tool default. Verified all four paths:

- direct call → `top_k=5` (tool default)
- pipeline without input → `top_k=5` (was `None`)
- direct `top_k=1` → `top_k=1`
- pipeline with `top_k=2` → `top_k=2`

## Tests

`TestAgentToolDefaultsThroughState` (4 tests): direct default, pipeline default, explicit direct value, explicit pipeline value. `test_pipeline_without_input_keeps_tool_default` fails on `main`. Full suite: `test/components/agents/test_agent.py` 136 passed, 2 skipped.

title: fix: keep tool argument defaults when an Agent state input is unset
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13680

### Proposed Changes:

`Agent` seeds its runtime `State` from the inputs that reach `run()`. Every state-schema key is also exposed as an optional component input with `default=None`, so a `Pipeline` passes `None` for the keys nobody wired. Those `None` values were seeded as state values, and tools that declare `inputs_from_state` then received `None` instead of their own argument defaults.

This change skips values that arrive as `None` when seeding the state, so an input that was never provided does not become a state value. `_inject_state_args` only injects keys that are present in the state, so the tool keeps its declared default. Explicitly provided values still take precedence over the default.

### How did you test it?

Added two unit tests in `test/components/agents/test_agent.py` (`TestAgentStateInputDefaults`):

- `test_pipeline_run_keeps_tool_default_when_state_input_is_unset` — a pipeline run without `top_k` now yields `top_k=5`.
- `test_pipeline_run_forwards_an_explicitly_provided_state_input` — passing `top_k=1` still yields `top_k=1`.

Red/green check: the first test fails on the unpatched source with `assert 'top_k=None' == 'top_k=5'` and passes with the fix.

Test results on the patched source:

- `test/components/agents/test_agent.py`: 134 passed, 2 skipped (the skips are the `OPENAI_API_KEY` integration tests).
- `test/components/agents/test_tool_calling.py` + `test/components/agents/test_state_class.py`: 124 passed.

End-to-end repro from the issue:

```
Agent alone          : top_k=5
Agent in pipeline    : top_k=5
Pipeline + top_k=1   : top_k=1
Agent alone + top_k=1: top_k=1
```

### Notes for the reviewer

The agent cannot distinguish "not provided" from "explicitly `None`" here, because both reach `run()` as `None` for these input sockets. This change treats `None` as "not provided", which is what a `Pipeline` sends for unconnected inputs. Non-`None` values are unaffected.

title: fix: handle non-finite scores in DocumentJoiner concatenate/merge modes and score sorting
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13678

### Proposed Changes:

`DocumentJoiner` no longer propagates non-finite (NaN) scores — the same class of hardening #13582 applied to `distribution_based_rank_fusion`, extended to the three sibling spots it did not cover:

- **`concatenate`** best-duplicate selection: a new `_ordering_score()` helper treats missing and NaN scores as `-inf` (comparisons against NaN are always `False`, which previously made the winner depend on arrival order — a NaN-scored duplicate that arrived first silently kept the "best duplicate" slot);
- **`merge`** weighted sum: reuses `_finite_score()` so a missing or non-finite score contributes 0 instead of turning the merged score into NaN;
- **final `sort_by_score`**: NaN-scored Documents are sorted as `-inf` (like `score=None` already was) instead of landing at arbitrary positions;
- each path logs a warning listing the affected Document IDs, mirroring the DBSF warning.

Unlike NaN, positive/negative infinity order correctly, so they keep their value for ordering (pinned by a test).

### How did you test it?

- New parametrized unit tests in `test/components/joiners/test_document_joiner.py` covering: NaN duplicate never wins (both arrival orders), all-NaN duplicates, merge with NaN/inf/-inf treated as 0, NaN sorted last, infinity still sorts first, and the three warnings (with Document ID assertions, modeled on the existing DBSF warning test).
- Full joiner suite: `pytest test/components/joiners/` — 131 passed.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on the changed files.
- Before/after verification script output (run against this branch) is quoted in the linked issue.

### Notes for the reviewer

- The `_finite_score` helper and the warning pattern are reused from #13582 as-is; `_ordering_score` is new because the "missing → 0" convention of `_finite_score` is right for arithmetic but wrong for ordering (where `None` already meant `-inf`).
- DBSF internally calls `_concatenate` on rescaled (finite) scores, so no double warnings from that path.

title: fix: keep in-memory BM25 statistics coherent during concurrent mutations
body:
### Related Issues

No existing issue found for this race.

### Proposed Changes:

Concurrent operations on an `InMemoryDocumentStore` can publish a document before its BM25 statistics are ready. An overlapping overwrite can leave the final content as `beta` while its statistics describe `alpha`, so searching for the stored content returns nothing. Deleting or clearing during a write can also leave orphan statistics and change later scores. Concurrent filter-based mutations can raise `RuntimeError: dictionary keys changed during iteration` or operate on a replacement document that no longer matches the filter.

Serialize `write_documents`, `delete_documents`, `delete_all_documents`, `delete_by_filter`, `update_by_filter` and `bm25_retrieval` with a reentrant lock owned by the index. The filter-based operations hold the lock from selection through mutation. Shared store instances use the same lock; non-shared stores keep their own. Reentrancy preserves the existing overwrite-to-delete and filter-to-delete call paths. Their async methods delegate to these protected methods, and independent indexes continue to run concurrently.

This incorporates [Aman Agnihotri's supplied fix](https://github.com/its-amann/haystack/commit/203399a2d620116615b240dfb17d6201a3426654), preserving its authorship, and extends its regression to cover both filter mutation methods.

### How did you test it?

- The regression tests cover overwrite/delete/clear, reads during writes, shared instances, custom async executors, and independent indexes.
- Against the previous PR head `087b6fe`, all four new filter-mutation cases failed with the dictionary-iteration error. With the follow-up fix, all four passed, covering deletion and metadata updates with both shared and non-shared stores.
- `hatch run test:unit test/document_stores/test_in_memory.py`: 416 passed, 8 skipped. The skips are existing optional index-recreation conformance cases; this backend has no `recreate_index` / `recreate_collection` parameter.
- `hatch run test:unit test/components/retrievers/test_in_memory_bm25_retriever.py`: 19 passed, 5 integration cases deselected.
- `hatch run test:integration test/components/retrievers/test_in_memory_bm25_retriever.py`: 5 passed, 19 unit cases deselected.
- Scoped `hatch run test:types` and `hatch run fmt-check` on the two Python files passed. All applicable pre-commit hooks passed on all three changed files.

All final checks ran on Python 3.12.14 and commit `1202fc9`. Full CI matrices, whole-tree checks, API-reference generation and Reno lint remain for CI; no remote CI result is claimed here.

### Notes for the reviewer

The original code and tests were generated with OpenAI Codex. This follow-up incorporates Aman's supplied patch and a Codex-authored test extension. Codex ran the reported checks; a separate Codex agent reviewed the frozen change.

The lock serializes the six methods listed above for the same index. Other read APIs and direct mutation of returned `Document` objects are outside this synchronization contract.

title: fix(sentence_tokenizer): Add support for Indic languages with danda sentence endings
body:
## Summary of Changes
Fixed the issue where `DocumentSplitter` with `split_by="sentence"` failed to recognize sentence boundaries in Indic languages (Hindi, Marathi, Bengali, etc.) that use the danda (`।`) or double danda (`॥`) as sentence endings. The fix adds support for these languages by:
1. Adding the missing language codes (hi, mr, bn, ne, pa, or, sa) to the `Language` Literal type and `ISO639_TO_NLTK` dictionary.
2. Creating a new `PunktLanguageVars` subclass that includes `।` and `॥` in `sent_end_chars`.
3. Ensuring this subclass is used for both `keep_white_spaces=True` and `keep_white_spaces=False` cases.

## Motivation & Context
Closes #13645

The issue affected several hundred million speakers of Indic languages. Without this fix, documents in these languages longer than the embedding model's input limit would be silently truncated, losing most of the content. The fix ensures proper sentence splitting for all supported languages.

## Verification
The fix can be verified by running the reproduction code from the issue description. For Hindi text with 6 sentences and `split_length=2`, the splitter should now produce 3 chunks instead of 1. Similarly, for Bengali and Marathi texts, the correct number of chunks should be produced.

title: fix(tools): validate and convert function tool arguments with the schema model
body:
Fixes #13659

## Problem

Function tools built their JSON schema from a Pydantic model but `Tool.invoke` called the function with the LLM's parsed JSON as-is — no conversion, no validation. Two consequences:

1. A parameter typed as a Pydantic model or dataclass (or `list[Model]`) received a plain `dict`, so the call failed even when the LLM sent arguments that match the advertised schema exactly (`ToolInvocationError: 'dict' object has no attribute 'qty'`).
2. Arguments that violate the tool's own schema were executed **silently**: `Literal["low", "high"]` accepted `"LOUD"`, `int` accepted `"3"`. The agent never got an error it could correct.

Both reproduced on `main` (8f75304) with the issue's scripts.

## Fix

`create_tool_from_function` already builds the Pydantic model to generate the schema — the fix keeps it:

- The model is stored on the `Tool` as `input_model` (a new dataclass field, excluded from `to_dict` so serialization is unchanged).
- `invoke` / `invoke_async` validate the arguments with `input_model.model_validate(...)` before calling the function: model/dataclass parameters arrive as **instances**, and schema violations raise `ToolInvocationError` carrying the pydantic validation message, so the LLM can retry with corrected arguments.
- Parameters injected from `inputs_from_state` are not part of the model (excluded from the schema at build time) and pass through untouched, as the issue suggests.
- `Tool.from_dict` rebuilds the model from the function signature after a round trip, so validation survives serialization.

Model building was factored into `_build_input_model` so the factory and the round-trip path share one implementation.

## Tests

New `TestArgumentValidationAtInvoke` in `test/tools/test_from_function.py` (6 tests): model params receive instances, schema violations raise `ToolInvocationError`, valid args unchanged, state-injected params pass through, async validation, and the serialization round trip. All **fail on `main`**, pass with the fix.

`pytest test/tools/`: 331 passed, 14 skipped.

title: fix: validate and convert function tool arguments before invoking
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13659

### Proposed Changes:

Tools created from functions (`create_tool_from_function` / `@tool`) build their JSON schema from the function's type hints, but `Tool.invoke` passed the LLM's parsed JSON to the function unchanged. Pydantic model and dataclass parameters received plain dicts, so every call failed, and arguments that broke the schema the tool advertised (a value outside a `Literal`, `"three"` for an `int`) ran silently.

- `Tool.invoke` / `Tool.invoke_async` now convert each argument that the Tool's schema exposes to the LLM against the type hint of the function's parameter, before calling it.
- The conversion is the one `ComponentTool` already uses (`from_dict` for types that have it, such as `Document` and `ChatMessage`, otherwise Pydantic `TypeAdapter`). I moved `ComponentTool._convert_param`'s body into `_convert_param_value` in `parameters_schema_utils.py` so both share it; `_convert_param` now delegates. The helper also unwraps `Annotated` before looking for `from_dict`, because function tools commonly use `Annotated[..., "description"]`; the `TypeAdapter` still gets the original type, so `Field` constraints in `Annotated` keep working.
- All invalid arguments are reported in one `ToolInvocationError`, one entry per field (for example `items.0.qty: Field required`), so the Agent can return the error to the LLM and let it retry with corrected arguments.
- Left untouched: arguments not in the schema (`State`, `inputs_from_state` values, streaming callbacks), parameters without a type hint, `*args`/`**kwargs` (so `ComponentTool`, whose invoker takes `**kwargs`, is not converted twice), and type hints Pydantic can't build a validator for.

### How did you test it?

- New unit tests in `test/tools/test_from_function.py` (`TestFunctionToolArgumentConversion`): Pydantic list, dataclass, `Annotated[list[Document], ...]` via `from_dict`, instances passed through, `"2"` coerced to `int`, invalid `Literal`/`int`/missing nested field reported together without calling the function, `Optional` with `None`, `State` and `inputs_from_state` values passed through, and the async path. 7 of these fail on `main` and pass with this change.
- New tests in `test/tools/test_tool.py` for a hand-written `Tool`: a type mismatch raises, and untyped or unexposed parameters and `**kwargs` are passed through.
- `pytest -m "not integration" test/tools test/components/agents` passes locally. The full non-integration suite has the same failures with and without this change (only tests that need optional dependencies I don't have installed), and `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` pass.

### Notes for the reviewer

- Behaviour change for hand-written `Tool`s: an argument exposed in the schema whose function type hint doesn't match now raises instead of being passed. I added an `upgrade` release note for this. If you'd rather limit the conversion to tools created from functions, I can store the flag on the Tool instead, but then deserialized tools would lose it, which is why I tied it to the function's own type hints.
- A `TypeAdapter` is built per call. Pydantic caches model schemas, so this is cheap for the usual tool sizes; I can cache adapters per Tool if you prefer.

title: fix: make Toolset copy the tools it receives
body:
### Related Issues

- No existing issue. I found this while auditing the code. Happy to open one if you prefer.

### Proposed Changes:

`Toolset` is a dataclass that stored the collection passed as `tools` by reference, which caused two problems:

- `Toolset.add()` appended to the caller's own list, and changing that list afterwards silently changed the `Toolset`:

  ```python
  tools = [tool_a]
  toolset = Toolset(tools)
  toolset.add(tool_b)
  tools  # [tool_a, tool_b]
  ```

- `add()` failed for any non-list iterable: `Toolset((tool_a,)).add(tool_b)` raised `TypeError: can only concatenate tuple (not "list") to tuple`.

`__post_init__` now copies the collection into a new list after the existing validation, so the `Toolset` owns its tools. Subclasses that pass `tools=[]` to `super().__init__()` and assign `self.tools` later (dynamic toolsets, `SearchableToolset`, `SkillToolset`) are not affected.

### How did you test it?

New tests in `TestToolsetAdd`: `add()` doesn't change the list passed to the constructor, changing that list doesn't change the `Toolset`, `add()` works after constructing from a tuple, and duplicate names are still rejected. The first three fail without the change and pass with it. `test/tools`, `test/components/agents` and `test/test_telemetry.py` pass (697 passed, 2 skipped). `ruff` and `mypy` are clean on the changed files.

title: fix: accept signed offsets in the Jinja2 {% now %} tag
body:
### Related Issues
- N/A (no existing issue found)

### Proposed Changes:
`Jinja2TimeExtension._get_datetime` built the shift amount by string concatenation: `float(operator + value.strip())`. For an offset value that already carries a sign — e.g. `{% now 'UTC' + 'hours=-2' %}` — that produced the literal `"+-2"` and raised `ValueError: could not convert string to float: '+-2'`, so the tag could not express a negative offset under an explicit `+`. The value is now parsed numerically first and the operator's sign is applied afterwards, so the operator and the value's own sign compose (`+`/`-2` -> -2, `-`/`-2` -> +2). An invalid operator is still rejected explicitly, preserving the previous `ValueError`.

Example now supported: `{% now 'UTC' + 'days=-1, hours=-2' %}`.

### How did you test it?
Added parametrized unit tests in `test/utils/test_jinja2_extensions.py` covering signed values under both `+` and `-`, signed multi-interval offsets, and equivalence of `{% now 'UTC' + 'hours=-2' %}` with `{% now 'UTC' - 'hours=2' %}`.

- `test/utils/test_jinja2_extensions.py`: 24 passed (was 17; the 7 new tests fail on the unpatched source with `could not convert string to float: '+-2'`).
- `test/utils` regression: 591 passed / 2 pre-existing environment failures (missing `torch` in `test_device.py`), identical on a clean tree (584 passed / same 2 failures).
- `ruff check` and `ruff format` clean.

### Notes for the reviewer
The explicit `operator not in ("+", "-")` guard is deliberate: a sign-multiplier-only implementation would silently accept an invalid operator and break the existing `test_invalid_operator`, so the invalid-operator contract is preserved rather than replaced.

title: fix: make MarkdownHeaderSplitter split_idx_start relative to the original document
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes n/a (no existing issue)

### Proposed Changes:

With `secondary_split` set, `MarkdownHeaderSplitter` keeps the `split_idx_start` that the secondary `DocumentSplitter` computes on each header section, so it is counted from the start of that section instead of the original document and restarts at 0 for every header. `SentenceWindowRetriever` orders context documents by `split_idx_start` when it merges them, so windows that span two sections come back out of order. For `"# Intro\nalpha beta gamma delta\n# Usage\nepsilon zeta eta theta\n"` with `split_length=2` and `window_size=1`, the window around the `epsilon` chunk is `"# Usage\nepsilon zeta eta delta\n"` instead of `"delta\n# Usage\nepsilon zeta eta "`.

The header split already tracks where each section starts in the original text (`source_start_idx`). The fix carries that offset through to the secondary split and adds it to each split's `split_idx_start`.

### How did you test it?

Only the secondary split path changes. Without `secondary_split` the splitter does not set `split_idx_start`, and `page_number` is unchanged.

title: fix: return empty string when RegexTextExtractor's first capture group does not participate
body:
### Related Issues

- Fixes #13484

### Proposed Changes:

**Problem.** `RegexTextExtractor` declares `captured_text: str`, but it returned `{"captured_text": None}` when the pattern matched and its first capture group did not take part in the match. Two examples: an alternation like `Score: (\d+)|N/A` matched against `"N/A"`, and an optional group like `Answer:( \w+)?` matched against `"Answer:"`. A downstream component then receives `None` where it expects a string.

**Cause.** `_extract_from_text` returned `match.group(1)` whenever the pattern had groups. Python's `re` returns `None` for a group that did not participate in the match.

**Fix.** Return `match.group(1) or ""`, so the result is `""` in that case. I picked `""` over falling back to the whole match (`group(0)`) because:
- the docstring says the component returns "the text captured by the first capturing group", and in this case that group captured nothing;
- `""` is already what the component returns when nothing matches, so callers can use one emptiness check;
- it is what the issue proposes and what the review on #13500 confirmed.

The `run` and `_extract_from_text` docstrings now describe this case. I also added a release note under `fixes`.

### How did you test it?

The repro script from the issue, run with `hatch -e test run python repro.py`:

```

{'captured_text': '7'}
{'captured_text': None}
{'captured_text': None}

# after
{'captured_text': '7'}
{'captured_text': ''}
{'captured_text': ''}
```

title: fix: split sentences ending with danda (।, ॥) in DocumentSplitter
body:
Fixes #13645.

NLTK's Punkt language vars only treat `.`, `?` and `!` as sentence ends. Hindi, Marathi, Bengali and other Indic text uses the danda (`।`, U+0964) and double danda (`॥`, U+0965), so `DocumentSplitter(split_by="sentence")` and `RecursiveDocumentSplitter` returned the whole document as one chunk.

This PR adds a `DandaPunktLanguageVars` class with those two characters added to `sent_end_chars`. `CustomPunktLanguageVars` now inherits from it, and `load_sentence_tokenizer()` uses it in place of the stock vars when `keep_white_spaces=False`. English output is unchanged.

Not changed: the `Language` Literal and `ISO639_TO_NLTK`. NLTK ships no Punkt model for these languages, so they still fall back to the English model, with the danda now handled.

Tests: added a parametrized regression test over both `keep_white_spaces` modes. `pytest test/components/preprocessors/` passes locally (533 tests, `integration` marker excluded).

title: fix: warn when MERGE combines two AND filters on the same field
body:
Fixes #13208

### Proposed Changes:

As agreed in the issue (option 2), two `AND` logical filters under `FilterPolicy.MERGE` keep being intersected, but this was silent when both had a condition on the same field, so e.g. init `meta.lang == "en"` plus runtime `meta.lang == "de"` returned no documents without any hint.

- `combine_two_logical_filters` now logs a warning naming the shared field(s) when both `AND` filters have conditions on the same field. The returned filter is unchanged.
- The `FilterPolicy.MERGE` comment, the `combine_two_logical_filters` docstring and the `apply_filter_policy` docstring now describe what actually happens (intersection for two `AND` filters, nesting under `AND` for two filters with the same other operator, the init filter ignored when operators differ, runtime precedence on the same field when a comparison filter is involved) instead of "runtime filters overwriting init values".
- Release note added.

### How did you test it?

- Two new unit tests in `test/document_stores/test_filter_policy.py`: same field keeps both conditions and warns (fails on `main`, no warning), different fields does not warn.
- `test/document_stores/test_filter_policy.py`: 18 passed. With the source file from `main`, the same-field warning test fails and the other 17 pass.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on the changed files.

title: fix: index snake_case-split tool name in SearchableToolset BM25
body:
## Description

The default BM25 tokenizer keeps `get_weather` as a single token, so a keyword that only appears inside a snake_case tool name was unreachable unless the tool description repeated it.

`SearchableToolset` built its BM25 index from `f"{tool.name} {tool.description}"`. Because the tokenizer treats `_` as a word character, a search for `weather` (when the description does not contain it) returned nothing for a tool named `get_weather`.

This change also indexes the tool name split on `_`, so `get_weather` is additionally indexed as `get weather` and a search for `weather` finds it. Exact-name and description-only matches are unchanged.

Fixes #13631

## Verification

Added `test_search_tools_matches_snake_case_name_word`: it builds a catalog where the keyword `flight` appears only inside the snake_case name `book_flight` (the description does not contain it) and asserts the tool is found. The new test fails before the change (`No tools found matching these keywords`) and passes after it; the existing `TestSearchableToolsetBM25Mode` suite continues to pass.

## AI disclosure

This change was developed with AI assistance. I have reviewed the diff and the added test and confirmed they pass locally.

title: fix: keep distribution-based rank fusion usable when a score is NaN or infinite
body:
Fixes #13581.

## The problem

`DocumentJoiner(join_mode="distribution_based_rank_fusion")` rescales each list with that list's mean and standard deviation. Both are computed from the raw scores, and `nan`/`inf` are contagious through them: one non-finite score makes `mean_score`, `std_dev`, `min_score`, `max_score` and `delta_score` all non-finite, so the rescaled score of *every* Document in the list becomes `NaN`. No exception, no log line — the pipeline looks healthy and the scores are unusable.

```python
docs = [Document(content="a", score=0.9), Document(content="b", score=0.5),
        Document(content="c", score=float("nan")), Document(content="d", score=0.2)]
DocumentJoiner(join_mode="distribution_based_rank_fusion").run([docs])["documents"]
# before: [('a', nan), ('b', nan), ('c', nan), ('d', nan)]
```

The mode already has a rule for a score that carries no ranking information: `score=None` is read as `0`, pinned by `test_run_with_distribution_based_rank_fusion_join_mode_with_none_score`. A `NaN` or an infinity is the same kind of unusable value, and reached this mode from custom retrievers, from a similarity function that divides by zero, and from embedding stores that return `nan` for a degenerate vector.

## The fix

One list comprehension, plus a warning when it fires:

```python
scores_list = [
    doc.score if doc.score is not None and isfinite(doc.score) else 0.0 for doc in documents
]
```

The rescaled values are then read out of `scores_list` instead of `doc.score`, so a Document with a non-finite score is rescaled from `0` rather than from `nan`. Nothing else changes: `scores_vary`, `delta_score` and the "all scores equal" branch still see the same numbers, and a list without non-finite scores produces the same numbers as before (pinned by `test_run_with_distribution_based_rank_fusion_join_mode_keeps_finite_scores`).

A warning is logged instead of a silent correction, so a retriever that emits `nan` can be found:

> Some of the Documents DocumentJoiner got have a non-finite score (NaN or infinity). It was configured with `distribution_based_rank_fusion`, so those Documents were treated as if their score were 0 to keep the scores of the other Documents usable.

With the fix the example above becomes:

```text
[('a', 0.74572), ('b', 0.54911), ('d', 0.40170), ('c', 0.30340)]
```

## Compatibility

- Documents that already came out of this mode with a finite score keep the exact same score; the arithmetic on `scores_list` is unchanged for finite input.
- `score=None` behaviour is untouched.
- The dropped information is only the relative position of the non-finite Document itself: it now lands at the bottom of the rescaled list instead of taking the whole list down with it. That is the ordering `None` scores already get.
- No new dependency: `isfinite` was already imported for the `weights` validation.

## Verification

Five tests added to `TestDocumentJoiner` in `test/components/joiners/test_document_joiner.py`, plus a reno note. Red/green, same machine, same interpreter, only the `scores_list` line swapped back:

```text
RED   (main)                      5 failed, 12 passed   -k "distribution_based and not weights"
  test_..._join_mode_with_nan_score
  test_..._join_mode_with_non_finite_score[nan]
  test_..._join_mode_with_non_finite_score[inf]
  test_..._join_mode_with_non_finite_score[-inf]
  test_..._join_mode_with_only_non_finite_scores

GREEN (this branch)               17 passed             -k "distribution_based and not weights"
GREEN (whole file)                52 passed, 7 deselected   -k "not merge_embeddings"
```

The `merge_embeddings` tests are deselected because they need a `Document` with `multivector_embedding`, which the released `haystack-ai` I ran against does not have yet; they fail identically before and after this change, and they do not touch this mode.

## Adjacent problems, not fixed here

- `sort_by_score` sorts `score=inf` to the top with no indication that the Document's score is not a real value — with this change such a Document is already `0.0` by the time it reaches the sort, so the case only survives for the other join modes.
- `_reciprocal_rank_fusion` (the RRF mode) ranks by position and ignores scores, so it never hits this; the `concatenate` and `merge` modes keep a non-finite score as-is.
- A `weights` list is rejected when it holds a non-finite value (`ValueError`), but that check is dead for this mode, since `weights` is documented as ignored here.

## Agent involvement

The reproduction, the patch and the tests were produced with an AI coding agent, and every number in this description comes from running the code on this branch. Reviewed by hand before pushing.

title: fix: `from_dict` must not deserialize into the caller's dictionary
body:
### Related Issues

- Relates to #13606 (`Tool.from_dict` mutates the caller's dictionary). `Tool` is deliberately **not** touched here — #13607 already covers it.

### Proposed Changes:

`default_from_dict` copies `init_parameters` before replacing serialized sub-objects with their instances. Its own comment says why:

> Copy so that replacing serialized sub-objects (Secret/ComponentDevice/nested components) with their deserialized instances below does not mutate the caller's `data` dict in place. Without this, a second deserialization of the same dict would receive already-parsed objects instead of their serialized form.

Sixteen components do their own deserialization into `data["init_parameters"]` **before** calling it, so that copy protects nothing. They all follow the same shape:

```python
init_params = data.get("init_parameters", {})     # reference, not a copy
init_params["splitting_function"] = deserialize_callable(...)   # writes into the caller's dict
return default_from_dict(cls, data)               # the copy inside is now pointless
```

Grouped by what ends up in the caller's mapping:

| Kind of handle | Components |
|---|---|
| callable | `DocumentSplitter`, `MockTextEmbedder`, `MockDocumentEmbedder`, `OutputAdapter`, `FunctionHook`, `LLM`, `Agent` (`streaming_callback`), `ChatPromptBuilder`, `FallbackChatGenerator` |
| enum | `DocumentWriter` (`DuplicatePolicy`), `InMemoryBM25Retriever` and `InMemoryEmbeddingRetriever` (`FilterPolicy`) |
| component / dataclass | `Agent` (`chat_generator`, `tools`), `LLM`, `FallbackChatGenerator`, `ToolResultOffloadHook` (`store`), `ConfirmationHook` (`confirmation_strategies`), `ComponentTool`, `PipelineTool` |

Three consequences, all covered by the new test:

1. the mapping handed in comes back modified — it holds live objects where the serialized handles were,
2. `json.dumps` on it now raises `TypeError`, so the payload can no longer be persisted,
3. deserializing the same payload a second time raises (`KeyError` / `TypeError` / `AttributeError`).

**Fix:** deserialize into a copy, and hand `default_from_dict` a fresh envelope that carries it.

For the two tool classes the change is smaller, because they build the instance directly from the mapping (`cls(**inner_data)`) rather than through `default_from_dict`, so copying the mapping is enough.

**Scope of the sweep.** I scanned every `from_dict` implementation in the repository (AST, tracking one level of aliasing through `data.get(...)` / `data[...]`) for writes into the caller's mapping before any rebinding to a fresh dict. It reported 17 sites; the one left out is `Tool`, which #13607 handles. The same defect has already been fixed one component at a time — MetadataRouter (#13421), MockChatGenerator (#13471), ListJoiner (#13563), all merged — so this closes the remaining instances rather than adding a fourth one-off. `Tool` is the last one left and is already claimed by #13607.

### How did you test it?

New file `test/core/test_from_dict_does_not_mutate.py` parameterises four components over the three invariants above (mapping unchanged, still JSON-serializable, second `from_dict` succeeds). Four cases cover the enum and nested-dataclass shapes: `DocumentWriter`, `InMemoryBM25Retriever`, `InMemoryEmbeddingRetriever`, `ChatPromptBuilder`.

I checked the test actually fails without the fix — reverting only `haystack/` and re-running the equivalent probe gives:

```
DocumentWriter: mutated=True, json=TypeError, second=KeyError
ChatPromptBuilder: mutated=True, json=TypeError, second=TypeError
```

and after the fix:

```
DocumentWriter: mutated=False
ChatPromptBuilder: mutated=False
```

Existing suites for the touched components: **297 passed, 36 failed**, and the same 36 fail on the unmodified tree (`git stash` baseline, identical set) — they need optional test dependencies (`transformers`, `sentence-transformers`) that are not installed here. No regressions.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on the changed files.

### Notes for the reviewer

- Each site gets the same four-line comment; it can be trimmed to one line if you prefer, but the reason is not obvious from `dict(...)` alone.
- `ChatPromptBuilder.from_dict` reads `data["init_parameters"]` rather than `.get(...)`, so a payload without that key still raises `KeyError` as before — behaviour unchanged.
- There is no shared helper for this yet. If you expect more components to appear, a `default_from_dict`-adjacent helper that takes the mapping and returns the envelope would remove the footgun; I did not add one because it would touch every component in this PR and make the diff harder to review.

title: fix: validate AnswerBuilder reference_pattern and raise a clear error for non-index matches
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13554

### Proposed Changes:

Previously, `AnswerBuilder` validated `pattern` to ensure it contained at most one capture group, but did not validate `reference_pattern`. When an invalid pattern was passed:
- A pattern with 0 capture groups (e.g. `r"\[\d+\]"`) caused `re.findall` to return full matches (e.g. `['[1]']`), crashing inside `_extract_reference_idxs` with `ValueError: invalid literal for int() with base 10: '[1]'`.
- A pattern with multiple capture groups (e.g. `r"\[(\d+)\]\[(\d+)\]"`) caused `re.findall` to return tuples of groups, crashing with `TypeError: int() argument must be a string, a bytes-like object or a real number, not 'tuple'`.
- This error remained silently hidden until a generator reply actually contained a citation.

**Solution:**
- Added `_check_reference_pattern(reference_pattern: str)` static method to validate that the compiled regex has exactly one capture group (`groups == 1`), raising a descriptive `ValueError` otherwise.
- Called validation in `run()` on the effective `reference_pattern` so invalid patterns are caught immediately, regardless of reply content.
- Updated `reference_pattern` docstrings in `__init__` and `run()`, and added `:raises ValueError:` documentation to `run()`.
- Added unit tests covering 0 capture groups, 2 capture groups, runtime overrides, and valid custom patterns.
- Added release note in `releasenotes/notes/`.

### How did you test it?

1. **Reproduction & TDD:** Verified failure before the fix and confirmed all cases (0 groups, 2 groups, runtime override) pass with the fix. Temporarily reverted the fix to ensure tests fail (`DID NOT RAISE ValueError`), then restored it.
2. **Quality Checks:**
   - **Linting & Formatting:**
     ```
     hatch run ruff check && hatch run ruff format --check
     ```

   - **Type Checking:**

     *Output:* `150 passed, 1 deselected in 15.22s`
3. **Pre-commit:** All pre-commit hooks passed cleanly on commit.

title: fix: stop PDF converters from mutating caller data in from_dict
body:
### Related Issues

None — I did not find an open issue for this, so I'm filing the fix directly together with the regression tests. Happy to open an issue first if you'd prefer.

### Proposed Changes:

`PyPDFToDocument.from_dict()` (`haystack/components/converters/pypdf.py:171`) and `PDFMinerToDocument.from_dict()` (`haystack/components/converters/pdfminer.py:154`) called `default_from_dict()` on a `dict` whose `init_parameters["link_format"]` they had **overwritten in place** with the deserialized `LinkFormat` enum. That mutates the caller's own dictionary, which breaks two things downstream:

- a second `from_dict()` on the same dict raises `AttributeError: 'LinkFormat' object has no attribute 'lower'` (`LinkFormat.from_str` in `haystack/components/converters/utils.py` calls `.lower()` on its argument), so cached or replayed serialized pipelines stop loading;
- the dict is no longer JSON-serializable, so anything that round-trips it through `json.dumps` fails with `TypeError: Object of type LinkFormat is not JSON serializable`.

The fix copies `init_parameters` before substituting the enum, so the caller's dict keeps the serialized string. This is the same pattern `BranchJoiner.from_dict()` (`haystack/components/joiners/branch.py:121-124`) already uses, and the same class of bug that #13563 fixed for `ListJoiner.from_dict()` (`haystack/components/joiners/list_joiner.py:100-105`).

title: feat: split MarkdownHeaderSplitter sections by token
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13600

### Proposed Changes:

`MarkdownHeaderSplitter` only offered `secondary_split="word" | "passage" | "period" | "line"`, so the only way to cap a chunk at a model's limit was to guess a words-to-tokens ratio. The secondary split already runs through `DocumentSplitter`, which has had `split_by="token"` for a while - the option just wasn't reachable from here.

So:

- `"token"` is now an accepted `secondary_split` value.
- New keyword-only `tokenizer_encoding: str = "o200k_base"`, forwarded to the inner `DocumentSplitter`. Same default as `DocumentSplitter` and `HierarchicalDocumentSplitter`, and, like them, only used when splitting by token.
- `warm_up()` already calls the inner splitter's `warm_up()`, so that is where tiktoken loads the encoding. `run()` warms up on its own the first time, so nothing changes for callers that don't call it.
- Header metadata, `split_id`, `page_number` and the page-break bookkeeping all go through the existing `_apply_secondary_splitting` untouched - token is just another unit for the inner splitter.

Kept this to `"token"`; `"sentence"` would be the same one-line change, but `DocumentSplitter`'s sentence splitter has its own defaults and I'd rather not bundle two behaviour changes into one PR. Happy to follow up if you want it.

### How did you test it?

Three unit tests in `test/components/preprocessors/test_markdown_header_splitter.py`:

- `test_secondary_split_by_token` - a header section with 400 words plus a second header with CJK text, `split_length=64, split_overlap=8`: every chunk is <= 64 tokens, both headers survive in metadata, `split_id` is contiguous.
- `test_secondary_split_by_token_uses_the_given_encoding` - `tokenizer_encoding="cl100k_base"` reaches the inner splitter.
- `test_tokenizer_encoding_is_unused_without_token_split` - word mode still behaves exactly as before and never touches tiktoken.

Both token tests are marked `integration` because tiktoken downloads the encoding on first use; they `importorskip("tiktoken")`.

```
pytest test/components/preprocessors
```

- before (base, only the source reverted): the two token tests fail with `unexpected keyword argument 'tokenizer_encoding'`
- after: `543 passed, 10 skipped`

`ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean on both files.

### Notes for the reviewer

The inner splitter is constructed with `tokenizer_encoding` unconditionally, not only in token mode. `DocumentSplitter` ignores it unless `split_by == "token"`, and threading it through unconditionally keeps `to_dict()`/`from_dict()` of this component symmetric - there's a test pinning that word mode is unaffected.

title: fix: Tool.from_dict must not deserialize into the caller's dictionary
body:
Closes #13606

## Problem

`Tool.from_dict` assigned `data["data"]` directly and replaced keys in place, so after the call the caller's dictionary held callables where the serialized handles were: `json.dumps(data)` raised `TypeError: Object of type function is not JSON serializable`, and a second `Tool.from_dict(data)` failed with `AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'split'`.

This is the same defect already fixed three times for other components: #13421 (`MetadataRouter`), #13471 (`MockChatGenerator`) and #13563 (`ListJoiner`).

`ToolCall`, `ToolCallResult` and `ReasoningContent` in `haystack.dataclasses.chat_message`, and `ToolCallDelta` and

title: feat: support secondary_split="token" in MarkdownHeaderSplitter
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13600

### Proposed Changes:

`MarkdownHeaderSplitter` can now split large header sections again by token count, so chunks fit the token
limit of an embedding model or LLM. It already uses `DocumentSplitter` for the secondary split, and
`DocumentSplitter` already supports `split_by="token"`, so this passes the option through. It mirrors
`HierarchicalDocumentSplitter` (#12917, #12919).

- `secondary_split` now also accepts `"token"` (requires `pip install tiktoken`).
- New keyword-only init parameter `tokenizer_encoding: str = "o200k_base"`, passed to the inner `DocumentSplitter`.
  It is only used when `secondary_split="token"`, and is serialized like the other init parameters. Pipelines saved
  before this change still load and get the default.
- `warm_up()` already warms up the inner splitter, so the tiktoken encoding is loaded there (or on the first `run()`).
- Header metadata, `split_id`, `source_id` and `page_number` work the same as for the other secondary split types.
- Docstrings, the docs page, and a release note are updated.

### How did you test it?

- 25 new unit tests in `test_markdown_header_splitter.py`. They use a fake tiktoken encoding (like the
  `DocumentSplitter` token tests), so they need no network. They cover:
  - init and defaults, and serialization, including a `Pipeline` round trip and old dicts without `tokenizer_encoding`
  - warm-up (encoding loaded once), and chunk size never above `split_length`
  - exact chunk contents and header metadata, with `keep_headers=False` too
  - `split_overlap` and `split_threshold` in tokens, and page numbers within and across sections
  - code blocks, documents without headers, empty documents, multiple input documents, and input meta
- 2 new integration tests with real tiktoken (`o200k_base`, `cl100k_base`). They check that every chunk is at most
  `split_length` tokens, the chunks rebuild the original text, and headers and page numbers are correct.
- `hatch run test:unit` and `hatch run test:integration` on the test file, ruff, and mypy all pass locally.

### Notes for the reviewer

The change in the component is small (one `Literal` value, one parameter, one argument passed through). Most of

title: fix: discard partial stream chunks from failed FallbackChatGenerator attempts
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13579

### Proposed Changes:

`FallbackChatGenerator.run` / `run_async` forwarded the caller's `streaming_callback` straight to every generator in the chain. When a generator streamed partial content and then raised, those chunks were already in the caller's hands; the next generator's chunks were appended to them, so the streamed text read `PARTIAL-from-A FULL-answer-from-B` while `replies[0].text` was just `FULL-answer-from-B`.

Both `_run_single_sync` and `_run_single_async` now buffer each attempt's stream into a local list and pass a simple `list.append` callback to the generator. The buffer is flushed to the caller's real callback only after the attempt succeeds. A failed attempt's partial chunks are discarded, so the caller only ever sees the stream from the generator that produced the final reply.

The async path uses `_invoke_streaming_callback` to flush, which handles both sync and async caller callbacks correctly.

### How did you test it?

Two regression tests using the issue's `FlakyGenerator` → `BackupGenerator` scenario:

- `test_streaming_partial_chunks_from_failed_attempt_are_discarded_sync` — verifies the sync path: a `_FlakyStreamGen` that streams `"PARTIAL-from-A "` and `"still-A "` then raises, followed by a `_DummySuccessGen(text="FULL-answer-from-B")`. Asserts `replies[0].text == "FULL-answer-from-B"` and that no chunk whose content contains `"PARTIAL"` or `"still-A"` reaches the caller.
- `test_streaming_partial_chunks_from_failed_attempt_are_discarded_async` — same assertions for `run_async`.

Added a `_FlakyStreamGen` mock component that streams partial `StreamingChunk`s and then raises, for both sync and async paths.

### Notes for the reviewer

- The buffering delays the caller's stream until the successful attempt completes. This is intentional: the streamed text must agree with the returned reply, and forwarding chunks from a potentially-failed attempt violates that invariant.
- Non-streaming calls (`streaming_callback=None`) are unaffected — `buffered_chunks` stays `None` and the code path is identical to before.
- `_invoke_streaming_callback` is imported from `haystack.dataclasses.streaming_chunk` for the async flush; it already handles the sync-callback-in-async-context case by calling the callback inline and awaiting only if the result is awaitable.

### Checklist

- [x] I have read the [contributors guidelines](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)
- [x] This PR was tested locally (unit tests added; existing streaming callback tests still pass conceptually)
- [ ] I have added tests that prove my fix is effective or that my feature works
- [x] I have updated the documentation if necessary (not needed — behavior change only affects error paths)

title: fix: keep pipeline snapshot file names valid on every platform
body:
### Related Issues

- none filed; this came up while running `test/core/pipeline/test_breakpoint.py` on Windows

### Proposed Changes:

`Pipeline.add_component` accepts component names that a file system rejects — it only rejects `.` and the reserved `_debug`. `_save_pipeline_snapshot` then built the snapshot file name from the raw name:

```python
file_name = f"{component_name}_{visit_nr}_{timestamp}.json"
```

On Windows that has two failure modes, both measured on Windows 11:

| component name | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `a\|b` | `OSError: [Errno 22] Invalid argument: '...\a\|b_0_2026_11_06_18_42_05.json'` | file `a_b_0_....json` |
| `ns:component` | snapshot written into an NTFS alternate data stream — `Path('ns:component_0_....json').exists()` is `True` and reading it back works, but the directory contains a single file named `ns`, so the snapshot is invisible and two component names sharing a prefix overwrite each other's stream | file `ns_component_0_....json` |
| `plain` | unchanged | unchanged |

The fix replaces `< > : " / \ | ? *` and control characters with `_`, and strips trailing dots and spaces (Windows drops those, which would make the file name differ from the one in the log). Names that are already legal are unchanged, so existing snapshots keep their names.

### How did you test it?

- New parametrized test `test_snapshot_file_name_can_be_created_on_any_filesystem`, covering `ns:component`, `a|b`, `a"b<c>d`, `a/b` and a plain name.
- On Windows 11 / Python 3.14.9, before the fix 4 of the 5 fail (`OSError` for `|`, wrong file name for `:`), `plain` passes; after the fix all 5 pass.
- `test/core/pipeline/test_breakpoint.py`: 46 passed.

### Notes for the reviewer

- Snapshot saving is opt-in via `HAYSTACK_PIPELINE_SNAPSHOT_SAVE_ENABLED`, so this only affects users of breakpoints — but for them the `:` case is silent, which is the worse half.
- I did not tighten `add_component`'s validation: rejecting these characters there would break names that work on Linux today.

AI assistance: the change and its tests were drafted with an AI assistant. I reviewed them and ran every test listed above on Windows.

title: fix: reject NaN scores in MetaFieldRanker linear_score mode
body:
### Related Issues

- No issue was filed for this one: it is a one-line fix in the same family as #13508 and #13410.

### Proposed Changes:

`MetaFieldRanker` in `linear_score` mode is meant to warn and default a document's score to 0 when that score is outside `[0, 1]`. The check read `document.score < 0 or document.score > 1`, and a `NaN` passes it — every comparison with `NaN` is `False`. The `NaN` therefore went into the weighted sum and became the sort key, so the document was ordered by a comparison that always evaluates to `False`. No exception, no warning.

The check is now `not 0 <= document.score <= 1`, the same form #13508 (`MetaFieldRanker` weight) and #13410 (`DocumentJoiner` weights) were changed to, for the same reason.

### How did you test it?

`test_linear_score_raises_warning_if_doc_wrong_score` was already parametrized with out-of-range scores; `float("nan")` is now one of them.

- Before the change: `1 failed, 4 passed` — only the `[nan]` case fails, because the warning is never logged.
- After the change: `test/components/rankers/` → `171 passed, 3 skipped`.

Manual check with three documents scored `nan, 0.9, 0.1`:

| | returned order |
|---|---|
| before | `nan` document first, score `nan`, no warning |
| after | `nan` document last, score `0.0`, existing warning logged |

### Notes for the reviewer

No behaviour change for valid scores. `inf` was already caught by the old check and still is; the guard is now written in the `not a <= x <= b` form the two recent NaN fixes use, so `NaN` cannot slip through again if the bounds change.

title: fix: treat a non-finite score as missing in DocumentJoiner DBSF mode
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13581

### Proposed Changes:

In `distribution_based_rank_fusion` mode, `DocumentJoiner` rescales the scores of each list with the mean and the standard deviation of that list, computed from the raw scores. A score that is `NaN` or infinite makes those two statistics non-finite, and with them the rescaled score of *every* Document in the list — the input looked fine, the output is all `NaN`, and nothing is logged or raised.

This PR treats a non-finite score the same way this mode already treats a missing one. `score=None` is already read as `0` in the same function (and pinned by `test_run_with_distribution_based_rank_fusion_join_mode_with_none_score`), so a new `_finite_score()` helper applies the same reading to `NaN`/`inf`, is used for both the statistics and the rescaling expression, and a single warning lists the ids of the affected Documents.

With the change, the reproduction from the issue (`[0.9, 0.5, nan, 0.2]`) returns `[0.7457…, 0.5491…, 0.4017…, 0.3034…]` in the original order instead of four `NaN`s, and a list made only of non-finite scores resolves to `0.0` rather than `NaN`.

The rescaling loop is written as an explicit loop over the already-computed scores instead of a comprehension that recomputed `doc.score if doc.score is not None else 0` twice; the arithmetic and the "all scores equal → keep original" branch are unchanged.

### How did you test it?

New unit tests in `test/components/joiners/test_document_joiner.py`:

- `test_distribution_based_rank_fusion_treats_non_finite_score_as_zero`, parametrized over `nan`, `inf`, `-inf`: asserts every output score is finite and that the finite Documents keep their relative order, with the non-finite one last
- `test_distribution_based_rank_fusion_handles_a_list_of_non_finite_scores`: a list made only of non-finite scores resolves to `0.0`

```text
python -m pytest test/components/joiners/test_document_joiner.py -q -k distribution_based_rank_fusion
15 passed

# same command with the two source files reverted to main:
4 failed (the four new cases), 11 passed
```

The full module in my local environment:

```text
python -m pytest test/components/joiners/test_document_joiner.py -q
61 passed, 2 failed
```

The two failures are `test_run_with_merge_embeddings_join_mode` and `test_merge_embeddings_rejects_conflicting_embeddings`, and they fail the same way on `main` without this change: they need the `merge_embeddings` mode, which postdates the Haystack 3.4.1 release my local environment is installed from (`Document.__init__() got an unexpected keyword argument 'multivector_embedding'`). CI runs them against `main` and they are untouched by this PR.

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on both changed Python files with the repository's `pyproject.toml`.

### Notes for the reviewer

- **Scope**: only the DBSF path is touched. `_concatenate` and `sort_by_score` are deliberately left alone — #12774 settled that deduplicating by the highest score is outside the contract, since an id is expected to identify the payload.
- **Reject vs. coerce**: the two merged fixes in this area (#13410 for `DocumentJoiner` weights, #13508 for the `MetaFieldRanker` weight) reject the invalid value at construction time. A score has no construction-time validation point, and raising in `run()` would turn a run that produces `NaN` today into a run that fails, so following the mode's existing `None` → `0` reading is the smaller change. If you'd rather have a `ValueError` collecting the offending ids (closer to `MaxSimRanker`, which rejects non-finite embeddings), say so and I'll switch it.
- **Warning**: emitted once per list, at `warning` level, mirroring how `sort_by_score` reports `score=None` handling. `None` scores stay silent because they are a legitimate state; a non-finite score is not.

title: fix: sort numeric metadata values numerically in get_metadata_field_unique_values
body:
### Related Issues

- N/A — no issue reports this. Found while reading `get_metadata_field_unique_values` against the
  `GetMetadataFieldUniqueValuesTest` mixin, which documents pagination over "a stable ordering".

### Proposed Changes

`InMemoryDocumentStore.get_metadata_field_unique_values` collects unique values keyed by
`(type(value).__name__, hashable_value)` and then ordered them by their string form:

```python
sorted_keys = sorted(unique_values, key=lambda k: (str(unique_values[k]), k[0]))
```

That is fine for keyword fields, but it is not monotonic for numbers — and the result is sliced by
`from_`/`size`:

```python
store.get_metadata_field_unique_values("n", from_=0, size=2)  # ([1, 10], 4)
store.get_metadata_field_unique_values("n", from_=2, size=2)  # ([2, 33], 4)
```

The second-smallest value `2` lands on page 2 while `10` is on page 1, so the page a caller receives
is not the page the ordering implies.

This sorts numbers numerically and keeps non-numbers ordered by their string form. The type name still
breaks ties, so `1` and `1.0` — which are distinct entries — keep a stable relative order across calls.

Scope: `InMemoryDocumentStore` only. The mixin in `haystack/testing/document_store.py` is shared with
the other document stores, so its pagination test keeps using a string field.

### How did you test it?

- Added `test_get_metadata_field_unique_values_sorts_numbers_numerically` to
  `test/document_stores/test_in_memory.py`; it asserts the full order and both pages.
- Reverted the ordering line locally and re-ran it: fails with
  `assert [1, 10, 2, 33] == [1, 2, 10, 33]`.
- Full file: `396 passed, 8 skipped`.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on both changed files: clean.

### Notes for the reviewer

- `#13071` also touches `count_unique_metadata_by_filter` in this file, but it changes the dedup key
  and does not overlap with the ordering line.

title: fix: skip invalid numeric indices in LLMRanker responses
body:
### Related Issues

No existing issue identified. Independently reproduced on `main` at `0de7bcdc0f0683b8a321197d635c5c39b6e804d0`; the affected source is unchanged at the updated base `63dcc3c4ee`.

### Proposed Changes:

`LLMRanker` converts model-response indices using `int()`. Given `{"documents": [{"index": 1.9}, {"index": 2}]}` and `top_k=1`, it therefore returns document 1 instead of skipping the invalid entry and returning document 2. Boolean indices can also select the wrong document, while `1e400` raises an uncaught `OverflowError`, even with `raise_on_failure=False`.

Skip boolean, fractional, and non-finite indices before conversion in the shared response parser. Preserve integer strings and integer-valued floats. If a nonempty ranking has no valid indices, use the existing fallback/error policy, including returning all fallback documents regardless of `top_k`.

Add regression tests for both execution paths and both failure policies, update the component documentation, and add a release note.

### How did you test it?

- Before the fix: 24 regression cases failed; 2 compatibility cases passed.
- After the fix: all 26 focused cases passed.
- After updating the base: the complete ranker unit-test module passed, **74 passed, 3 integration tests deselected**.
- Focused mypy, Ruff lint/format checks, applicable pre-commit hooks on the four changed files, and `git diff --check` passed.

The tests use `MockChatGenerator` and require no GPU, model download, or API key. I ran the checks locally with Python 3.12.3. Full-repository tests, repository-wide type checking, live-provider integration tests, and the documentation-site build were not run.

### Notes for the reviewer

This validates model-produced JSON in a parser that already skips unusable indices. It preserves existing valid input handling, including `"2"` and `2.0`. The tests inject malformed responses deterministically; they do not measure their frequency with a live provider.

AI tools were used to help draft and organize this contribution. I reviewed the final changes and ran the local checks; I remain responsible for their correctness.

title: fix: reject required underscore-prefixed tool parameters
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13472

### Proposed Changes:

`create_tool_from_function` and `@tool` built tool schemas with Pydantic `(annotation, default)` fields. Pydantic treats a name that starts with `_` as a private attribute, so a parameter such as `_tenant` never appeared in `model_json_schema()`. When that parameter was required, the model could not supply it and `Tool.invoke` failed with a missing argument.

Underscore-prefixed parameters stay out of the schema. They are not exposed to the LLM. If a required parameter (no default) starts with `_` and is not covered by `inputs_from_state`, tool creation now raises `ValueError` and names the parameter. The check runs after the existing `inputs_from_state`, `State`, and `Callable` skips. Supply the value with `inputs_from_state`, or give the parameter a default.

```python
tool = create_tool_from_function(lookup_order, inputs_from_state={"tenant": "_tenant"})
```

Parameters that already have a default are still omitted from the schema, and the function keeps that default. `create_tool_from_function` and `@tool` document this.

The earlier change that kept these names in the schema with a Pydantic alias is removed, including the `ComponentTool` and dataclass schema changes from that approach.

### How did you test it?

- `hatch run fmt`: ruff checks passed
- `hatch run reno lint .`: passed
- `hatch -e test run pytest -m "not integration" test/tools/test_from_function.py test/tools/test_component_tool.py test/tools/test_parameters_schema_utils.py -q --no-cov`: 93 passed, 2 skipped, 7 deselected
- New tests: a required `_tenant` raises; the same function succeeds when `_tenant` is in `inputs_from_state` and `_tenant` stays out of the schema; a defaulted `_tenant` stays out of the schema while `invoke()` uses the default.

### Notes for the reviewer

This follows the direction from @sjrl on issue #13472: do not expose `_` parameters to the LLM, and fail at tool creation only for a required underscore parameter that `inputs_from_state` does not cover.

`ComponentTool` is unchanged from main.

This change was AI-assisted. I have reviewed the changes and run the relevant tests.

- [x] I have read the [contributors guidelines](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and the [code of conduct](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/blob/main/code_of_conduct.txt).

title: docs: document that XLSXToDocument row numbering assumes the pandas positional index
body:
### Related Issues

- N/A

### Proposed Changes

`XLSXToDocument` numbers the rows of the output table from 1 so that they match the Excel row numbers:

    df.index = df.index + 1

That only holds when pandas assigns the positional index. Supporting every combination of `read_excel_kwargs` in the converter is out of scope, so this documents the limitation in the `read_excel_kwargs` docstring instead, following the `CSVDocumentSplitter` wording.

The added paragraph states that:

- options that shift the rows or replace the index, such as `skiprows` or `index_col`, make the numbering inaccurate;
- a source whose `index_col` holds non-numeric values is skipped;
- the conversion output should be validated on representative inputs when these options are customized.

Behavior is unchanged — the diff is docstring only.

### How did you test it?

No behavior change, so no new test. I checked that the documented behavior is what `main` actually does:

| input | result |
|---|---|
| `index_col` on a string column | 0 documents, warning `can only concatenate str (not "int") to str` |
| `index_col` on a numeric column with a header row | 0 documents, same warning (the header text lands in the index) |
| `index_col` on a numeric column without a header row | rows renumbered `101, 102` → `102, 103` |
| `skiprows=2` | rows numbered from 1 instead of the Excel row numbers 3, 4 |

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` report the same results as on unmodified `main` for this file.

### Notes for the reviewer

- Dropped the test and the release note from the earlier revision; the branch is now a single docstring commit based on `0de7bcdc`.
- The `index_col` failure above is a separate pre-existing defect. Happy to send a follow-up that guards only that case if you'd rather fix it than document it.

Fixes #13507.

\MetaFieldRanker\ documents \weight\ as being in \[0, 1]\, but the check \weight < 0 or weight > 1\ is false for \NaN\, so a NaN weight passed validation and both \eciprocal_rank_fusion\ and \linear_score\ returned documents with \NaN\ scores.

ot 0 <= weight <= 1\ rejects NaN and infinities while keeping the existing error message and the valid bounds 0 and 1 unchanged. The constructor and the \un()\ override share the same validation, so both paths are covered.

title: fix: stop ListJoiner.from_dict from mutating the caller's data
body:
### Related Issues

N/A — no open issue reports this component. The pattern is discussed on #13420 (which tracks `MetadataRouter`), and no PR there touches `ListJoiner`.

### Proposed Changes

`ListJoiner.from_dict` wrote the deserialized type back into the dictionary it was given:

```python
data["init_parameters"]["list_type_"] = deserialize_type(data["init_parameters"]["list_type_"])
```

so a single deserialization corrupts the caller's serialized data. `haystack/core/serialization.py` deliberately avoids exactly this in `default_from_dict` (copy first, *"so that replacing serialized sub-objects ... does not mutate the caller's `data` dict in place. Without this, a second deserialization of the same dict would receive already-parsed objects"*), and #12935 applied the same treatment to `BranchJoiner.from_dict` and `ConditionalRouter.from_dict`, and #13471 to `MockChatGenerator.from_dict`. `ListJoiner` is the joiner that was missed.

Observable consequences of the current behaviour, on a pristine `main`:

```
serialized list_type_ : 'list[haystack.dataclasses.chat_message.ChatMessage]'
caller dict now holds : list[haystack.dataclasses.chat_message.ChatMessage]
caller dict unchanged?: False
caller dict still JSON-serializable: NO -> TypeError : Object of type GenericAlias is not JSON serializable
2nd from_dict same dict: FAILED -> TypeError : can only concatenate str (not "types.GenericAlias") to str
```

The fix copies `init_parameters` (and the enclosing mapping) before substituting the deserialized type, mirroring `BranchJoiner.from_dict`, so the caller's data stays serialized and can be loaded again.

### How did you test it?

New regression test `TestListJoinerDeserialization::test_from_dict_does_not_mutate_caller_data` — asserts through the public round trip (`to_dict()`/`from_dict()`) that the caller's dict keeps its serialized string, stays JSON-serializable, and deserializes twice. It fails on `main` and passes with the patch.

Baseline, unmodified `main` (`965b5bd`), test file untouched:

```
collected 20 items
============================= 20 passed in 1.42s ==============================
```

BEFORE — test added, source untouched (`git status --porcelain` showed only `M test/components/joiners/test_list_joiner.py`):

```
>       assert data["init_parameters"]["list_type_"] == serialized_type
E       AssertionError: assert list[haystack.dataclasses.chat_message.ChatMessage] == 'list[haystack.dataclasses.chat_message.ChatMessage]'

test\components\joiners\test_list_joiner.py:29: AssertionError
=========================== short test summary info ===========================
FAILED test/components/joiners/test_list_joiner.py::TestListJoinerDeserialization::test_from_dict_does_not_mutate_caller_data
======================== 1 failed, 20 passed in 2.10s =========================
```

AFTER — with the patch, same file:

```
============================= 21 passed in 1.39s ==============================
```

AFTER — same demo against the patched source:

```
caller dict unchanged?: True | value: 'list[haystack.dataclasses.chat_message.ChatMessage]'
caller dict still JSON-serializable: YES
2nd from_dict: list[haystack.dataclasses.chat_message.ChatMessage]
```

No regressions in the surrounding suites:

```
test/components/joiners/ + test/core/pipeline/breakpoints/test_pipeline_breakpoints_list_joiner.py
============================= 117 passed in 1.63s =============================
test/core/pipeline/test_breakpoint.py
============================= 41 passed in 0.53s ==============================
```

Quality gates on the two changed files:

```
ruff check   -> All checks passed!
ruff format --check -> 2 files already formatted
mypy         -> Success: no issues found in 2 source files
release_note_backticks.py --check -> exit 0
```

Run with Python 3.11.15 / pytest 9.2.0 / mypy 2.4.1 / ruff 0.16.0 against the source tree at `965b5bd` (`PYTHONPATH` pointed at the checkout, import resolution verified by printing `haystack.components.joiners.list_joiner.__file__`). I did not use `hatch` for these runs, so the environment is close to but not identical to the CI matrix.

Updates `github/codeql-action/init` from 4.39.1 to 4.39.2
Release notes

Sourced from github/codeql-action/init's releases.

v4.39.2

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

See the releases page for the relevant changes to the CodeQL CLI and language packs.

[UNRELEASED]

No user facing changes.

4.39.2 - 03 Nov 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.4. #4284
  • Upcoming breaking change: CodeQL version 2.22.3 and earlier were discontinued on 16 October 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.18, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. Added a deprecation warning for customers using these versions of CodeQL. #4266
  • Starting with macOS 27 and Xcode 27, traced analyses are unsupported. See this blog post for more information. The CodeQL Action will now try to identify if a workflow is about to perform a traced analysis on version 27 or above of macOS or Xcode. If so, the CodeQL Action will emit a corresponding warning that will also be visible on the Tool Status Page. This check will be rolled out following this release of the CodeQL Action. #4221
  • The undocumented TRAP cache cleanup feature that could be enabled using the CODEQL_ACTION_CLEANUP_TRAP_CACHES environment variable has been removed, as announced in the release notes for CodeQL Action 4.35.2. The analyze Action now warns if this environment variable is set. If you used TRAP cache cleanup to limit Actions cache usage, we recommend disabling TRAP caching by passing the trap-caching: false input to the init Action. #4243

4.39.1 - 21 Oct 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.3. #4256

4.39.0 - 15 Oct 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.20.7. #4205
  • The codeql-action/analyze step now validates that a correct argument for the checkout_path input has been provided. The checkout_path input must be set to the path where the repository that is being analyzed is checked out at on the runner, if that path is something other than the workspace root. If the path does not point to a repository checkout or is different from the path that was used by codeql-action/init, then the CodeQL Action now produces a warning. #4148

4.38.3 - 08 Oct 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.2. #4203

4.38.2 - 24 Sept 2026

  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.1. #4160

4.38.1 - 18 Sept 2026

  • The CodeQL Action now has experimental support for CodeQL releases for which per-language bundles are available. Per-language bundles support analysis for a single language and are therefore smaller than the combined bundles that allow analysis for all supported languages. As a result, per-language bundles take up less space on disk and are faster to download. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in the coming weeks. #4146

4.38.0 - 09 Sept 2026

  • On GitHub-hosted runners, the CodeQL Action now deletes unused CodeQL bundles from the toolcache before downloading a different bundle, which frees up disk space for the analysis. We expect to roll this change out to everyone in September. #4124
  • The CodeQL Action now supports CodeQL releases that are compatible with Linux Arm64 and downloads the native linux-arm64 CodeQL bundle when available. #4072
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.27.0. #4129

4.37.9 - 26 Aug 2026
