title: fix: validate AnswerBuilder reference patterns
body:
### Related Issues

Fixes #13554. The report and runtime-only validation direction are from that issue.

### Proposed Changes

Validate the effective `reference_pattern` in `AnswerBuilder.run()`, after applying the runtime override and range-pattern resolution. Require exactly one capture group and report invalid regex syntax with a contextual `ValueError`. Empty captures and integer-conversion failures also identify the reference pattern and document index.

Validation stays out of `__init__`, so a placeholder or invalid initialization value can still be replaced at runtime. title: docs: clarify that word_count_threshold counts whitespace-separated words, not tokens
body:
## What

Documentation-only change to `LostInTheMiddleRanker`: the docs now spell out what `word_count_threshold` actually counts. No behaviour change.

## Why

`word_count_threshold` is computed with `str.split()`, so it budgets whitespace-separated chunks, not model tokens. Users reasonably read "words" as a proxy for the downstream context window, but a URL, a hash, or a code expression counts as one word no matter how many tokens a tokenizer splits it into, and code-heavy or non-Latin text needs noticeably more tokens per word than English prose. A threshold sized for a model's context window can therefore still overflow it.

@julian-risch offered exactly this follow-up in #11351:

> If you have a suggestion how to improve the docstring to make this limitation more clear, feel free to open a PR.

## Changes

- `__init__`: the paragraph describing the threshold now states the counting unit.
- `__init__` and `run()`: `:param word_count_threshold:` explain `str.split()`, what counts as a single word, and that the value is an approximate budget rather than a context-window guarantee.
- Adds a release note.

## Verification

- `python -m py_compile` on the modified file passes.
- No line exceeds the repository's `line-length = 120`.
- The diff touches docstrings only; no executable statement changes.

No tests added: no executable code changed.

Refs #11351

title: fix(rankers): reject non-finite MetaFieldRanker weights
body:
Fixes #13507

## Problem

`MetaFieldRanker` documents `weight` as a value in `[0, 1]`, but the existing validation only checks:

```python
if weight < 0 or weight > 1:
```

For `NaN`, both comparisons are false, so `float("nan")` is accepted by the constructor and by the `run()` override. Subsequent reciprocal-rank or linear-score fusion produces `NaN` scores instead of rejecting the invalid input. Infinite values should also be rejected explicitly.

## Changes

Use `math.isfinite(weight)` alongside the existing range check. This applies to both constructor validation and run-time weight overrides because both paths use `_validate_params`.

## Tests

Added coverage for `NaN`, positive infinity, and negative infinity:

- constructor rejects each non-finite value
- `run(weight=...)` rejects each non-finite override

```
pytest test/components/rankers/test_metafield.py -q
57 passed
```

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on both touched files: passed.

title: fix: preserve To, Cc, and Bcc recipient types in MSGToDocument
body:
### Related Issues

Fixes #13392

### Proposed Changes

Previously, `MSGToDocument` placed all recipient-table entries on the `To:` line, regardless of their recipient type. Additionally, messages without transport headers lost their separate `Cc:` and `Bcc:` lines.

This PR fixes recipient classification and formatting by:

- Grouping recipients by `PidTagRecipientType` while preserving their original order and formatting.
- Prioritizing existing `Cc:` and `Bcc:` transport headers when present.
- Independently falling back to recipient-table entries when the corresponding headers are missing.
- Ignoring documented resend flags when classifying recipient types.
- Excluding originator entries and recipients with missing or unsupported types instead of incorrectly assigning them to `To:`.

The component documentation and release note have also been updated to describe the corrected behavior and upgrade implications.

### How did you test it?

**Environment:**
- Python 3.12.10
- `python-oxmsg` 0.0.2
- Windows

**Validation results:**
- Confirmed that 9 regression cases failed before applying the fix.
- **MSG converter tests:** 17 passed, covering header precedence, missing and empty headers, recipient ordering, resend flags, and unsupported recipient types.
- **Repository-wide type checking:** Passed across 566 files.
- **Scoped Ruff checks:** Passed.
- **Applicable pre-commit hooks:** Passed.

**Not run:**
- Full unit test suite
- Documentation-site build

### Notes for the Reviewer

Thanks to @L4XB for reporting the issue and providing a [prepared fix](https://github.com/L4XB/haystack/tree/fix/msg-recipient-types), and to @ishasparkhe for #13394.

title: fix: accept messages from other providers in OpenAIResponsesChatGenerator
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13465 (Responses side, Bedrock side in deepset-ai/haystack-core-integrations#4183)

### Proposed Changes:

- When `FallbackChatGenerator` switches from another provider (e.g. `AmazonBedrockChatGenerator`) to `OpenAIResponsesChatGenerator`, the history contains assistant messages the Responses API rejects:
  - Reasoning without a Responses reasoning item `id`/`type` was sent as `{"summary": [...]}`, which the API reads as a message with role `''` (400).
  - Tool calls without `extra["call_id"]` were sent with their own `id` (e.g. `tooluse_...`, API expects `fc...`) and an empty `call_id` (400).

- `OpenAIChatGenerator` already ignores reasoning, so it needs no change.

### How did you test it?

New parametrized unit test, plus a manual run against `gpt-5-nano` with Bedrock-shaped text and tool-call histories (all three previously returned 400, now succeed).

Tool-call formatting moved into `_convert_tool_call_to_responses_api_format` to keep `_convert_chat_message_to_responses_api_format` under the complexity limits.

title: fix: raise ValueError on negative top_k in InMemoryDocumentStore retrieval
body:
### Related Issues

No open issue tracks this. I found it while checking whether the `top_k` validation added at the retriever layer in #12719 also protects the document store underneath it — it does not.

### Proposed Changes:

**Cause.** `InMemoryDocumentStore.bm25_retrieval()` and `InMemoryDocumentStore.embedding_retrieval()` forward `top_k` straight into a `[:top_k]` slice (`haystack/document_stores/in_memory/document_store.py:811` and `:902` on `main`). Python interprets a negative bound as "drop this many from the end", so an invalid argument silently returns a shortened, wrong ranking instead of failing:

```text
10 matching documents, top_k=-1  -> 9 returned
10 matching documents, top_k=-3  -> 7 returned
10 matching documents, top_k=-8  -> 2 returned
```

`bm25_retrieval_async()` / `embedding_retrieval_async()` delegate to the synchronous methods through `run_in_executor`, so all four entry points were unguarded — while `InMemoryBM25Retriever` / `InMemoryEmbeddingRetriever` already raise `ValueError` for the same input since #12719.

**Fix.** Add the same guard to both synchronous methods, reusing the retriever message verbatim (`top_k must be greater than or equal to 0, but got {top_k}`), and extend the two `:raises ValueError:` docstring lines. Behaviour for non-negative values is unchanged, including `top_k=0`, which still returns no documents.

### How did you test it?

Four new tests in `test/document_stores/test_in_memory.py`, parametrized over `top_k in [-1, -5]` and covering both synchronous and both asynchronous entry points (16 test cases across the shared / not-shared store classes).

Before the guard — pristine `document_store.py`, new tests in place:

```console
$ python -m pytest test/document_stores/test_in_memory.py -k "negative_top_k" -q
16 failed, 386 deselected in 0.86s
E   Failed: DID NOT RAISE ValueError
```

After the guard:

```console
$ python -m pytest test/document_stores/test_in_memory.py -k "negative_top_k" -q
16 passed, 386 deselected in 0.15s
```

Whole file, plus the consumer side (both retrievers and `SearchableToolset`):

```console

$ python -m pytest test/components/retrievers/test_in_memory_bm25_retriever.py \
                  test/components/retrievers/test_in_memory_embedding_retriever.py \
                  test/tools/test_searchable_toolset.py -q
102 passed, 2 skipped in 1.78s
```

Lint / type / release-note checks on the changed files:

```console
$ ruff check haystack/document_stores/in_memory/document_store.py test/document_stores/test_in_memory.py
All checks passed!
$ ruff format --check <same two files>
```

title: fix: stop sentence overlap once split_overlap words are reached
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13521

### Proposed Changes:

`DocumentSplitter._number_of_sentences_to_keep` stopped sentence overlap only when the running word count was strictly greater than `split_overlap` (`if num_words > split_overlap`). A sentence that already contained exactly `split_overlap` words did not stop the loop, so the sentence before it was kept as well. The comparison is now `>=`.

For `split_length=6` and `split_overlap=2` on `Alpha beta. Gamma delta. Epsilon zeta. Eta theta.`, the second chunk was `Gamma delta. Epsilon zeta. Eta theta.` (four overlapping words). It is now `Epsilon zeta. Eta theta.`

- Longer sentences stay whole. The sentence is counted before the comparison, so a sentence longer than `split_overlap` is not cut to the overlap size.
- The first sentence of the current chunk is still skipped (`reversed(sentences[1:])`), so the next chunk is not a copy of the current one.
- While the running count is still below `split_overlap` (`word_count_overlap < split_overlap`), another sentence can still be added. That matches Haystack 1.26.4 `_get_overlap_from_slice`, which adds a sentence only while `word_count_overlap < split_overlap`.

### How did you test it?

- Added `test_sentence_overlap_stops_when_word_count_is_exact`: it fails on `main`
  (second chunk `Gamma delta. Epsilon zeta. Eta theta.`) and passes with this change.
- `hatch run test:unit test/components/preprocessors/test_document_splitter.py --no-cov -q` — 85 passed, 11 deselected
- `hatch run fmt-check` and `hatch run test:types` on the changed files — clean
- Pre-commit hooks pass on all three changed files.

### Notes for the reviewer

Small change. Chunk text changes only when the count lands exactly on split_overlap. This PR was developed with the help of an AI assistant. I have reviewed and understand the changes.

title: fix: attempt remaining pipeline cleanup after component errors
body:
### Related Issues

No linked issue. Reproduced through public Pipeline resource-lifecycle calls with actual local file resources; the related tool-batch cancellation work in #12796 concerns a different owner.

### Proposed Changes:

If one component's `close()` raises, pipeline cleanup currently exits before visiting later components. Repeating cleanup can encounter the same error and leave those later resources open again.

Attempt all remaining cleanup hooks after an ordinary `Exception`, then re-raise the first exception object. Preserve component order, native async cleanup preference and sync fallback. Cancellation and other `BaseException` subclasses still interrupt immediately; the pipeline cannot repair resources inside a component whose own cleanup fails. The pipeline guide and Reno release note describe that behavior.

### How did you test it?

- The original owner fails 9 new lifecycle cases while 12 controls pass. The sync/async/lifecycle selection passes all 76 tests after the change, with two existing Document-mutation warnings.
- A public Pipeline consumer reproduces a genuine buffered-file `EFBIG` cleanup error; later files remain open on base and close after the patch, while the same error propagates.
- A separate agent review exercises 42 fresh public cases, including genuine `EBADF`, exception identity/cause/traceback, repeated calls, mixed async/sync cleanup and real task cancellation. The base misses later cleanup in 12 cases; the patch passes.
- Scoped Hatch formatting, selected-file pre-commit hooks and mypy for both Python files pass. The branch hook is checked on the publication branch. No full test environment, repository suite, documentation-site build or live integration is claimed.

title: fix: preserve tool deserialization input
body:
### Related Issues

- No tracked issue; same defect class as #13420 (MetadataRouter, fixed in #13421) and the just-merged #13471 (MockChatGenerator): `from_dict()` mutating the caller's serialized configuration.

### Proposed Changes:

`Tool.from_dict()`, `ComponentTool.from_dict()`, `PipelineTool.from_dict()`, and `AgentTool.from_dict()` deserialized in place, writing the result back into the dictionary supplied by the caller:

- `Tool.from_dict()` replaced `data["data"]["function"]` / `["async_function"]` with the resolved callables and rewrote `data["data"]["outputs_to_state"]` / `["outputs_to_string"]` handlers with live callables.
- `ComponentTool.from_dict()` / `AgentTool.from_dict()` replaced `data["data"]["component"]` / `["agent"]` with the live component instance, and `PipelineTool.from_dict()` popped `is_pipeline_async` and rewrote the `outputs_to_*` configs inside the caller's dict.

Consequences of one `from_dict()` call on a user-held dictionary:

- the dictionary no longer holds serialized data, so it fails `json.dumps`/`yaml.dump` and no longer compares equal to `tool.to_dict()`;
- calling `from_dict()` on the same dictionary a second time crashes with `AttributeError: 'function' object has no attribute 'split'` inside `deserialize_callable()` — this also hits `Toolset.from_dict()` and `deserialize_tools_or_toolset_inplace()`, which pass their nested tool dictionaries straight to `Tool.from_dict()`.

The fix deserializes a copy instead (shallow copy of the tool parameters; `deepcopy` of the nested serialized component/agent, because the nested component's own `from_dict()` also rewrites its `init_parameters` in place), so the caller's dictionary keeps the serialized configuration and can be loaded more than once. This mirrors what `BranchJoiner.from_dict()` ("Copy so the caller's data keeps the serialized type and can be deserialized again") and the merged `MockChatGenerator.from_dict()` fix (#13471) already do.

The `parameters=inner_data.get("parameters", None)` → `get("parameters")` adjustments in `ComponentTool.from_dict` are `ruff --fix` (SIM910) output: the copied dict is now statically a `dict`, which newly triggers the rule on those lines.

### How did you test it?

- New regression tests (one per class) assert that after `from_dict(data)` the input still equals its deep-copied snapshot and that a second `from_dict(data)` succeeds:
  - `test/tools/test_tool.py::TestToolAsync::test_from_dict_preserves_input`
  - `test/tools/test_component_tool.py::TestComponentToolInAgent::test_from_dict_preserves_input`

title: fix: keep code on the same line as a docstring in PythonCodeSplitter
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13308

### Proposed Changes:

With `strip_docstrings=True`, `PythonCodeSplitter` removes a docstring by dropping its whole source lines. When code follows the docstring on its closing line, for example `"""Docs."""; return 5`, that code was silently lost and the chunk was no longer valid Python.

- `_strip_docstring` now checks the text after the docstring on its closing line (using `end_col_offset`). If anything other than a comment is there, the docstring is kept in the content instead of being stripped. This follows the existing check that skips stripping when the docstring shares a line with the `def`/`class`.
- A trailing comment (`"""Docs."""  # note`) is still stripped as before, since dropping it loses no code.
- Applies to functions, methods, classes and class headers, since they all go through `_strip_docstring`.

### How did you test it?

- Added a parametrized test for code on the docstring line (function, multi-line docstring, method, class header). It checks that the code is kept, the docstring stays in the content, and every chunk still parses with `ast.parse`.

title: fix: keep code that shares a line with a docstring in `PythonCodeSplitter`
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13308

### Proposed Changes:

`PythonCodeSplitter._strip_docstring` removes a docstring by dropping whole source lines (`after = source_lines[ds_end:unit_end]`). When the next statement starts on the docstring's last line, as in `"""Docs."""; return 5`, that statement was dropped too. title: fix: resolve string field annotations of dataclasses in ComponentTool schemas
body:
### Related Issues

- Related to #12950 (closed as not planned). There, `ComponentTool(component=AnswerJoiner())` failed because `ExtractedAnswer` annotates its offsets as `Optional["Span"]`. The issue was closed because there is no clear Agent use case for `AnswerJoiner`, with the note that the schema-generation problem was still useful to have identified. The same bug hits user-defined dataclasses, which is what this PR fixes. As a side effect, `AnswerJoiner`'s schema now builds.
- #13095 took the same approach (resolve the annotations with `get_type_hints`, break cycles with a `ForwardRef`) but was closed automatically before any review because its CLA wasn't signed. This PR is an independent implementation. It also falls back to the annotations as written when they can't be resolved, and it replaces references back to a dataclass inside other typing constructs too, such as `Annotated` and `tuple`, so recursive dataclasses keep their current schema.
- This is the dataclass counterpart of #12739, which resolved postponed annotations for function tools.

### Proposed Changes:

`ComponentTool` documents dataclass inputs ("Dataclasses (both simple and nested structures)"), but creating the tool fails when a dataclass has string field annotations. Two common patterns hit this:

1. A quoted forward reference to a dataclass defined later in the module, such as `items: list["Item"]`.
2. A dataclass in a module that uses `from __future__ import annotations`, with a field typed as `date`, an `Enum`, `Optional[...]`, `Literal[...]` or another dataclass.

```python
from dataclasses import dataclass

from haystack import component
from haystack.tools import ComponentTool

@dataclass
class Order:
    items: list["Item"]

@dataclass
class Item:
    sku: str

@component
class OrderCounter:
    @component.output_types(count=int)
    def run(self, order: Order) -> dict:
        """
        Count the items of an order.

        :param order: The order.
        """
        return {"count": len(order.items)}

ComponentTool(component=OrderCounter())
# >> SchemaGenerationError: Failed to create JSON schema for the run method of Component 'OrderCounter'
# >> caused by PydanticUserError: `run` is not fully defined; you should define `Item`, then call `run.model_rebuild()`.
```

Such a component can't be wrapped as a tool, and so can't be given to an `Agent`, unless its parameters schema is written by hand.

**Cause:** `_dataclass_to_pydantic_model` passed string field annotations to `pydantic.create_model` unchanged. It only walked non-string annotations through `_resolve_type`, so forward references nested in typing constructs (such as `Optional["Span"]`) stayed unresolved too. Pydantic then looked those names up in the namespace of `haystack.tools.parameters_schema_utils`, where `create_model` is called. Builtins and the names this module happens to import (such as `Annotated`, `Any`, `Union`, `Sequence`, `ChatMessage`) resolved by accident, and Pydantic resolved a dataclass's reference to itself to the model being built; anything else, including the user's other classes, failed.

**Fix** (in `haystack/tools/parameters_schema_utils.py`):

- The field annotations are resolved with `typing.get_type_hints(cls, include_extras=True)`, that is, in the module and class namespace that define the dataclass. `include_extras=True` keeps `Annotated` metadata such as `Field(min_length=1)`. If the annotations can't be resolved (for example, a name imported only under `TYPE_CHECKING`), the annotations are used as written, which is the current behavior. This mirrors `_resolve_parameter_types` in `haystack/core/type_utils.py`.
- Resolved annotations need care for recursive dataclasses: resolving `children: list["Node"]` to the real class would make `_resolve_type` recurse forever, and a real class left inside `Annotated` or `tuple` would make Pydantic add a second definition of the dataclass. So `_dataclass_to_pydantic_model` now passes down an immutable set of the dataclasses whose conversion is in progress (there is no module-level state). Before a field type is resolved, the new private helper `_replace_back_references` turns every reference to one of them into `ForwardRef("<name>")`, which Pydantic resolves to the model being built. It does this at any depth, in `list`, `Optional` and `dict` as well as in `Annotated`, `tuple` or `Mapping`, which `_resolve_type` passes to Pydantic unchanged. Type hints without such references are returned as they are. Recursive dataclasses that work on main therefore produce the same schema as before.
- The `ChatMessage` handling in `_resolve_type` is unchanged, and the existing schema tests for Haystack's dataclasses (`Document`, `ChatMessage`, `ToolCall`, and others) pass unmodified. A `ChatMessage` field with a string annotation now goes through it as well; see the notes for the reviewer.

There are no public API changes.

### How did you test it?

- I added tests to `test/tools/test_component_tool.py`, next to the existing dataclass tests. They use module-level dataclasses with string annotations, which is what `from __future__ import annotations` turns every annotation into. This is the same approach as the test in #12739.
  - `test_from_component_with_postponed_dataclass_annotations` has fields annotated `"Annotated[str, Field(min_length=1)]"`, `"date"`, an `Enum`, `"Literal['open', 'done']"` and `"list[Address]"`. It asserts the full schema (`minLength`, `format: date`, the enum under `$defs`, the `$ref`s). It also checks that `invoke()` turns the nested dicts into a `date`, an enum member and `Address` instances.
  - `test_from_component_with_forward_referenced_dataclass` uses `items: list["OrderItem"]`, with `OrderItem` defined after `Order`, and asserts the schema and `invoke()`.
  - `test_from_component_with_recursive_dataclass` uses `children: list["TreeNode"]`.
  - `test_from_component_with_recursive_dataclass_in_annotated_and_tuple` uses a `Category` dataclass with `subcategories: "Annotated[list[Category], Field(max_length=20)]"`, `related: tuple["Category", ...] = ()` and `parent: "Category | None" = None`. It asserts the full schema, with a single `Category` entry under `$defs` that keeps Haystack's field descriptions, `maxItems` and the default, and checks `invoke()`.
- The first two tests fail on main with `SchemaGenerationError` (`you should define date` and `you should define OrderItem`) and pass with the fix. The two recursive tests pass on main too and guard the recursion handling. If the references inside `Annotated` and `tuple` aren't replaced, the last test gets two module-qualified definitions of `Category`, one of them generated by Pydantic without Haystack's field descriptions.
- I ran `pytest -m "not integration"` on `test/tools`, `test/components/agents`, `test/core`, and the OpenAI and Azure chat generator tests (`test_openai*.py`, `test_azure*.py`), which build `ComponentTool` schemas. Compared test by test with main, the only difference is the four new passing tests. Two limits of my environment:
  - Four `test/core` modules that import pandas or pytest-bdd were not collected.
  - `test_serialization_security.py::TestModuleAttributeWalkBypass::test_callable_walk_through_reexported_unallowlisted_class_rejected` fails on both main and this branch because `rich` is not installed.
- I compared the generated tool schemas with main's, as JSON:
  - Every dataclass in `haystack.dataclasses` (as a parameter, as `list[...]` and as `... | None`), every built-in component that can be created with default arguments, and 15 more common components created with simple arguments: the schemas are identical, except that `AnswerJoiner` and `ExtractedAnswer` now build. I fixed `PYTHONHASHSEED` for this, because `PromptBuilder` orders its inputs by set iteration.
  - 56 dataclass shapes, most of them recursive: references back to the dataclass inside `list`, `Optional`, `dict`, `Sequence`, `Annotated`, `tuple` and `Mapping`, mutual references and three-cycles, both with quoted annotations and in a `from __future__ import annotations` module. The 31 shapes that build on main give byte-identical schemas with the fix. 23 shapes fail on main and build with the fix, and 2 fail on both (the shape in the first note below, and a `Callable` field).
- `test/tools` passes, and both schema comparisons give the same results, on Python 3.11 with pydantic 2.14.2 and with pydantic 2.12.0, the minimum version in `pyproject.toml`.
- I also ran a script that uses a real `from __future__ import annotations` module with `date`, `Enum`, `Literal`, `Optional` and nested-dataclass fields. Creating the `ComponentTool` fails on main and works with the fix, and `invoke()` returns the converted values. With the fix, `ComponentTool(component=AnswerJoiner())` from #12950 also builds its schema, with `Span` under `$defs`.
- `pre-commit run --files` passes on the changed files, and mypy reports no issues for them.

I tested on Windows with Python 3.12, plus Python 3.11 for `test/tools` and the schema comparisons.

### Notes for the reviewer

- Mutually recursive dataclasses (A <-> B, or A -> B -> C -> A) now work too, because Pydantic also resolves the outermost model under construction by name. Two limits remain. On main, these shapes either fail or already produce the same schema.
  - A dataclass that refers back to two different ancestors at once (X -> Y -> Z, where Z points to both Y and X) still raises `SchemaGenerationError`. Pydantic only sees the model being built and the outermost one. To keep the change small, I didn't add a model registry for this case, but I can add one if you think it's worth it.
  - `_resolve_type` still leaves a dataclass inside `Annotated`, `tuple` or `Mapping` to Pydantic. So if A reaches B only through such a construct and B refers back to A, the schema builds, but B and a second definition of A come from Pydantic, without Haystack's field descriptions.
- #13473 edits the same loop in `_dataclass_to_pydantic_model`, so whichever of the two PRs lands second needs a small rebase.
- #13311 adds an `Annotated` branch to `_resolve_type` that calls `_resolve_type(args[0])`. The two PRs only conflict in the test imports: `parameters_schema_utils.py` merges cleanly, so nothing flags that call. Whichever of #13311 and this PR lands second needs to pass `converting=converting` there. Without it, dataclasses that refer to each other only through `Annotated` fields recurse until `RecursionError`. A dataclass that refers to itself inside `Annotated` is not affected, because its references are replaced before `_resolve_type` descends.
- One schema changes for dataclasses that already worked on main. A `ChatMessage` field with a string annotation (for example in a `from __future__ import annotations` module) used to resolve by accident to Pydantic's own `ChatMessage` schema, with `_role`, `_content`, `_name` and `_meta`. It now gets the same schema as a `ChatMessage` field without a string annotation: `role`, `content`, `name` and `meta`. `invoke()` converts a dataclass input that has no `from_dict` with Pydantic's `TypeAdapter`, which expects the underscored names for a nested `ChatMessage`, so arguments that follow this schema fail, as they already do on main when the annotation isn't a string. I kept that conversion out of this PR, but I can fix it here or in a follow-up.

title: fix: resume legacy snapshots whose paused component has an empty socket
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13488

### Proposed Changes:

Resuming a legacy breakpoint snapshot (`inputs_format=None`) crashes with `IndexError: list index out of range` as soon as the paused component has an input socket with no stored value. A legacy snapshot stores inputs flattened and without senders, so `_consume_component_inputs` treats every socket as "already consumed" and hands the paused component the first value of each socket queue. When a socket is empty (a component with only optional inputs started without any input, or any optional socket left out of the snapshot) that queue is `[]`, and `socket_inputs_values[0]` raises.

The fix only puts a socket into `consumed_inputs` when there is something to restore. Sockets left out are then filled by `_add_missing_input_defaults`, which runs right after `_consume_component_inputs` in `Pipeline.run` and gives the component the default declared on the socket - the same thing that happens when the component is called without that input.

I considered passing `None` instead, but that would override a socket default of `"hi"` with `None` and fail component validation, so leaving the socket untouched is what gives the "resume with its default" behavior the issue asks for.

### How did you test it?

Two unit tests in `test/core/pipeline/test_breakpoint.py` under `TestResumeFromLegacyPipelineSnapshot`, both building the legacy snapshot literally, like the existing legacy tests do:

- `test_resume_from_legacy_snapshot_with_empty_socket`: the paused component has a single optional input and the snapshot holds `{'greeter': {}}`.
- `test_resume_from_legacy_snapshot_with_one_empty_optional_socket`: the snapshot holds `{'greeter': {'greeting': 'hello'}}`, so a stored value still wins over the default.

Without the change the first test fails with `IndexError: list index out of range` at `haystack/core/pipeline/base.py:1357`. With it both pass, and the current-format resume tests are unaffected.

```
$ pytest -q test/core/pipeline/test_breakpoint.py
43 passed

$ pytest -q test/core/pipeline --ignore=test/core/pipeline/features
478 passed, 4 skipped, 2 failed
# both failures (`test_merge_super_component_pipelines`, `test_find_super_components`)
# fail the same way on 8e38c63 without this patch
```

`test/core/pipeline/features` needs extras that are not installed here, so it was not run. Release note included.

### Notes for the reviewer

- I only had the legacy snapshot shape from the issue description, so the tests build it by hand instead of deriving it from a current snapshot. Worth a look that this matches what older snapshot files actually contain.
- The same empty-queue guard could be applied outside the resume branch (a queue holding only `_NoOutputProduced` has the same effect), but I left that out to keep the diff small.

title: fix: let Pipeline.connect match Union and Literal members in any order
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13509

### Proposed Changes:

`_strict_types_are_compatible` compared the members of two `Union` types, and the values of two `Literal` types, by position. A connection passed only when each sender member matched the receiver member at the same position: `str | None` connected to `str | None | int`, but not to `str | int | None`.

A `Union` sender is now compatible when each of its members is compatible with the receiving `Union`, which reuses the existing branch for a non-union sender. A `Literal` sender is compatible when all of its values are in the receiving `Literal`. A release note describes the change.

### How did you test it?

New cases in `test/core/test_type_utils.py`:

- compatible: `Literal["b", "c"]` to `Literal["a", "b", "c"]`, `Optional[str]` to `Union[int, str, None]`, `str | None` to `str | int | None`, and `list[Path | ByteStream]` to `list[str | Path | ByteStream]`. All four fail on main. The existing reverse-direction test checks each of them the other way round, where they stay incompatible.
- incompatible: `Literal["a", "x"]` to `Literal["a", "b", "c"]`. It fails if the `Literal` check accepts a sender with only some of its values in the receiver; the existing partially overlapping union cases do the same for the `Union` check.

`test/core` passes (1893 passed), except `test_show_in_notebook`, which needs IPython, not installed in my environment. It fails the same way on main. mypy on `type_utils.py` and the pre-commit hooks pass.

title: fix: don't let system reminders reset StructuredOutputHook retries
body:
### Related Issues

- No issue. Follow-up to #13359, which added `StepBudgetReminderHook` and the `system_reminder` marker.

### Proposed Changes:

HUMAN: While trying the new `StepBudgetReminderHook` from #13359 alongside `StructuredOutputHook`, I noticed `max_retries` stops working. The reminder is posted as a user message, and the structured-output hook counts retries back to the last user message, so every reminder resets the count and the agent keeps asking for corrections until `max_agent_steps`. Compaction already skips these reminders, so I made the retry count skip them too, and added tests with the reminder on every step and at its default setting.

`StructuredOutputHook` counts the correction messages it added since the last user message, and stops counting at the
first user message without its correction tag. `StepBudgetReminderHook` adds each reminder as a user message marked
`meta={"system_reminder": True}`. Once reminders start, there is a reminder between the latest correction and the
new reply, so `_count_corrections` returns 0 every time and `max_retries` never applies. The Agent keeps sending
corrections until `max_agent_steps`, and the run ends with `exit_reason="max_agent_steps"`.

`_count_corrections` now skips user messages carrying the `system_reminder` marker, the same way compaction already
does (`_is_real_user_message`). A real user message still starts a new turn.

| | main | this PR |
|---|---|---|
| `max_retries=1`, `max_agent_steps=6`, `StepBudgetReminderHook(remind_within_steps=6)` | 6 LLM calls, 6 corrections, `max_agent_steps` | 2 calls, 1 correction, `text` |
| 7 tool steps then prose, `max_agent_steps=10`, default reminder | 10 calls, 3 corrections, `max_agent_steps` | 9 calls, 1 correction, `text` |

### How did you test it?

- Two new unit tests in `test/hooks/structured_output/test_hooks.py`: an Agent run with both hooks (asserts 2 steps,
  1 correction, `exit_reason == "text"`) and a direct `_count_corrections` test with interleaved reminders (a real
  user message still resets the count). Both fail on `main` and pass here.
- `test/hooks` and `test/components/agents` pass (the only failures, `TestRichConsoleUI`, also fail on `main` in my env).
- `hatch run fmt` / ruff and mypy on the changed module are clean. Only `MockChatGenerator`, no LLM calls.

title: fix: count each source once in reciprocal rank fusion
body:
### Related Issues

Found through code inspection; no linked issue.

### Proposed Changes

Reciprocal-rank fusion counts repeated occurrences of a document ID within one input list as separate votes. This can happen when retrieval results are concatenated before fusion, for example when two store-backed queries feed `ListJoiner` and its output becomes one `DocumentJoiner` input; the duplicates can inflate that source's contribution.

Track seen document IDs independently for each source and count only its first occurrence. Preserve the existing source weights, rank positions and final document selection.

Duplicate IDs within one source no longer multiply its contribution. Documents returned by different sources still receive one vote from each source.

### How did you test it?

Validation on base `3165374708ea57a0115bd506358b3a56db1aa2d2`:

New regressions reproduce the duplicate-source voting defect on the unchanged source. The selected document-joiner tests pass after the fix: 142 passed, 6 deselected. Hatch formatting, scoped mypy and git diff --check passed.

Reproduction: `python -m pytest -q test/components/joiners/test_document_joiner.py`.

These results were recorded on the stated base revision; they are not a fresh run against subsequently advanced main.



Current-head verification (`a7ffc42d`, base `965b5bdd`): a native Pipeline with two `InMemoryBM25Retriever` outputs, `ListJoiner`, and `DocumentJoiner` reproduces the duplicate contribution and its effect on weighted ordering. The PR counts one contribution per document ID in each input list, preserves the original rank positions, and leaves the direct two-source control unchanged. The [current upstream Tests run](https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/actions/runs/41958279512) passed unit/integration checks on Linux, macOS and Windows, along with formatting and type checks. title: fix: serialize pydantic models in JSON mode so snapshots with datetime fields can be saved
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13490

### Proposed Changes:

`_serialize_value_with_schema` stored pydantic models with `model_dump()`, which keeps Python objects such as `datetime`, `date`, `UUID` and `Decimal`. `_save_pipeline_snapshot` then failed in `json.dump`, so with `HAYSTACK_PIPELINE_SNAPSHOT_SAVE_ENABLED` set the breakpoint raised `TypeError: Object of type datetime is not JSON serializable` instead of `BreakpointException`, and left a half-written snapshot file behind.

title: fix: resume legacy breakpoint snapshots with empty sockets
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13488

### Proposed Changes:

`_consume_component_inputs()` handles resuming a breakpoint snapshot by taking the first stored value for each input socket. A legacy snapshot (`inputs_format=None`, written by an older Haystack) may not carry a value for every socket of the paused component, for example when all of its inputs are optional. The resume branch indexed `socket_inputs_values[0]` without checking the list, so such a snapshot raised `IndexError: list index out of range` instead of resuming the component with its defaults.

The fix leaves a socket without a stored value out of the consumed inputs, matching the non-resume convention where missing sockets are filled with their defaults. Sockets that do carry values keep the existing behaviour (regular, greedy and lazy-variadic sockets are unchanged). A regression test covers a legacy snapshot of an all-optional component, and a release note is added.

### How did you test it?

title: perf: speed up pipeline input deep copies for Documents and immutable values
body:
### Related Issues

- n/a (performance improvement, no linked issue)

### Proposed Changes:

The pipeline deep-copies component inputs with `_deepcopy_with_exceptions` in `haystack/core/pipeline/utils.py`. For inputs with embeddings, most of that time goes into per-element overhead. This PR makes two changes; copies are as deep as before.

- **`Document.__deepcopy__`.** `Document` now implements `__deepcopy__`. Like the default `deepcopy`, it creates the instance without `__init__`, registers the copy in the memo, and deep-copies every attribute. The one difference is that an `embedding` that is a `list` is copied in one step instead of element by element; its floats are immutable, so the result is still a full deep copy. An `embedding` of any other type (for example a NumPy array set after construction) is deep-copied as before. Subclasses keep their type. Because this lives on `Document`, every `deepcopy` of a Document gets faster, not just pipeline input copies.
- **Immutable built-ins return early in `_deepcopy_with_exceptions`.** `None`, `bool`, `int`, `float`, `complex`, `str` and `bytes` (exact type only) are returned as-is, as `deepcopy` would do. Before, every leaf value went through the `isinstance(obj, (Component, Tool, Toolset))` check, and `Component` is a `runtime_checkable` `Protocol`, so that check is slow. It ran once per float of a raw embedding list such as `query_embedding`. Subclasses of these types still go through the regular path, so a custom `__deepcopy__` on them is still used.

### How did you test it?

**Unit tests.**

- `test/dataclasses/test_document.py`, `deepcopy(document)`:
  - equal to the original, same type, same attributes, and every mutable attribute is a new object, for Documents with embeddings, nested `meta`, `blob` and `sparse_embedding`;
  - mutating nested `meta` in the copy leaves the original unchanged;
  - an embedding list shared with `meta` stays shared in the copy (in both attribute orders) and is not the original list;
  - extra instance attributes are deep-copied;
  - a NumPy `embedding` stays a NumPy array and is copied;
  - a `Document` subclass keeps its type, and its own fields are copied;
  - copying neither triggers the in-place mutation warning nor changes the `id`.
- `test/core/pipeline/test_utils.py`, `_deepcopy_with_exceptions`:
  - immutable built-ins return the same objects `deepcopy` returns;
  - a `str` subclass with a custom `__deepcopy__` still uses it.

`hatch run test:unit` passes, and mypy and ruff are clean.

**Benchmark.** This times `_deepcopy_with_exceptions` (and plain `deepcopy` in the last row) on `main` and on this branch, each run in its own process, since `Document.__deepcopy__` changes `deepcopy` itself (Python 3.14, macOS, min of 7 runs). The script is below.

| Input | `main` | this PR | speedup |
|---|---|---|---|
| `query_embedding` (list of 768 floats) | 1.08 ms | 0.022 ms | 48.6x |
| 200 Documents, 768-dim embeddings | 5.34 ms | 0.720 ms | 7.4x |
| 200 Documents, 1536-dim embeddings | 9.77 ms | 0.964 ms | 10.1x |
| 200 Documents, no embeddings | 0.784 ms | 0.566 ms | 1.4x |
| prompt inputs (10 strings) | 0.015 ms | 0.001 ms | 23.3x |
| `deepcopy` of a list of 200 Documents, 768-dim | 5.03 ms | 0.417 ms | 12.1x |

These timings measure copying alone.

**Real pipelines.** To see the effect with a real model, I ran real pipelines over the Haystack docs (481 Markdown files → 2,481 chunks) with `BAAI/bge-base-en-v1.5` (768-dim) on an Apple GPU. The embedder components call `sentence_transformers` directly, since that integration is no longer in core. `main` and this branch ran in separate processes, alternating twice, with 3 runs each per process; values are medians of the 6 runs per version. Time inside `_deepcopy_with_exceptions` is measured directly. No LLM was called; the query pipeline ends at `ChatPromptBuilder`.

| Workload | Time in `_deepcopy_with_exceptions` (`main` → this PR) | Total pipeline time (`main` → this PR) |
|---|---|---|
| Indexing: `DocumentSplitter` → embedder → `DocumentWriter` | 116 ms → 42 ms | 42.6 s → 42.5 s |
| 100 queries: embedder → `InMemoryEmbeddingRetriever` (top 5) → `ChatPromptBuilder` | 129 ms → 9 ms | 4.39 s → 4.29 s |

Copy time is the reliable number. End-to-end, the change saves about 1.2 ms per query, roughly 3% of a 44 ms query in this setup. For indexing, the embedding model dominates and the 75 ms saved is within run-to-run noise. With an LLM call in the query pipeline, the relative gain shrinks further. This PR reduces Haystack's own per-component overhead; it does not make model-bound pipelines noticeably faster.

<details>
<summary>Benchmark script</summary>

Run it once against a checkout of `main` and once against this branch:

```bash
git worktree add /tmp/haystack-main main
hatch -e test run python bench.py /tmp/haystack-main
hatch -e test run python bench.py "$(pwd)"
```

```python
import random, sys, timeit

sys.path.insert(0, sys.argv[1])
import haystack
from copy import deepcopy

from haystack import Document
from haystack.core.pipeline.utils import _deepcopy_with_exceptions as f

assert haystack.__file__.startswith(sys.argv[1]), haystack.__file__

random.seed(0)
emb = lambda n: [random.random() for _ in range(n)]
cases = {
    "query_embedding (list of 768 floats)": (f, {"query_embedding": emb(768)}),
    "200 Documents, 768-dim embeddings": (f, {"documents": [Document(content="x" * 500, embedding=emb(768), meta={"page": i}) for i in range(200)]}),
    "200 Documents, 1536-dim embeddings": (f, {"documents": [Document(content="x" * 500, embedding=emb(1536), meta={"page": i}) for i in range(200)]}),
    "200 Documents, no embeddings": (f, {"documents": [Document(content="x" * 500, meta={"page": i, "tags": ["a", "b"]}) for i in range(200)]}),
    "prompt inputs (10 strings)": (f, {f"k{i}": "text " * 50 for i in range(10)}),
    "deepcopy of a list of 200 Documents, 768-dim": (deepcopy, [Document(content="x" * 500, embedding=emb(768), meta={"page": i}) for i in range(200)]),
}

def t(fn, x):
    n = max(1, int(0.2 / min(timeit.repeat(lambda: fn(x), number=1, repeat=3))))
    return min(timeit.repeat(lambda: fn(x), number=n, repeat=7)) / n * 1000

for name, (fn, x) in cases.items():
    print(f"{name}: {t(fn, x):.3f} ms")
```

</details>

### Notes for the reviewer

- As suggested in review, the Document fast path now lives in `Document.__deepcopy__` instead of the pipeline utility, so the exclusion attributes, the `copyreg` check and the guard test are gone.
- One deviation from the suggested snippet: it checks `type(value) is list` rather than `value is not None`, so a non-list `embedding` (such as a NumPy array assigned after construction) keeps its type instead of becoming a `list`.
- Since `Document` now defines `__deepcopy__`, a reducer registered for `Document` with `copyreg` is no longer used by `deepcopy`; that is standard Python precedence for classes with `__deepcopy__`.

title: fix!: clean before splitting in DocumentPreprocessor
body:
Related Issues

- fixes #13480

Proposed Changes:

DocumentPreprocessor split documents first and cleaned each chunk afterwards. The splitter computes split_idx_start and _split_overlap for the raw chunks, and the cleaner then rewrote the content (stripping and collapsing whitespace) and, with the default keep_id=False, gave each chunk a new ID. The metadata no longer matched the returned chunks: overlap entries referenced IDs that didn't exist, and split_idx_start didn't match the content. SentenceWindowRetriever uses these fields to rebuild context windows, so it glued words together ('one twothree four') or duplicated characters ('one twoo threee').

This PR swaps the order: DocumentCleaner runs first on the whole document, then DocumentSplitter splits the cleaned text, so IDs, split_idx_start and _split_overlap are computed on the final content.

- The cleaner always keeps the input document's ID, so source_id on each chunk still refers to the input document. As a result keep_id no longer has an effect; the parameter is kept for compatibility and its docstring says so.
- remove_repeated_substrings now sees the whole multi-page document, which is what its header/footer detection expects.
- Chunks now keep the splitter's whitespace (for example 'one two three four '), the same as DocumentSplitter output on its own.

How did you test it?

- Added test_run_split_metadata_refers_to_returned_chunks: exact ordered chunk content and split_ids, split_idx_start as a character range into the cleaned text, source_id pointing to the input document, and every _split_overlap entry resolving to a returned chunk. It fails on main and passes with this change.
- Updated test_init for the new input/output mapping, and the cleaned-content check in test_run, which previously required stripped chunks.
- Ran the repro from #13480 end to end with InMemoryDocumentStore and SentenceWindowRetriever: windows now match the cleaned text exactly, with and without overlap.
- hatch run test:unit on test/components/preprocessors/ and test/components/retrievers/test_sentence_window_retriever.py (536 passed), ruff check, ruff format and hatch run test:types.

Notes for the reviewer

This changes output for existing users (chunk content keeps trailing whitespace, chunk IDs change, keep_id has no effect), so I added an upgrade release note with migration steps and used fix! in the title. If you'd rather keep keep_id meaningful or deprecate it formally, I'm happy to adjust.

title: fix: keep system reminders in SlidingWindowCompactor
body:
### Related Issues

- No issue. Follow-up to #13359, which added `StepBudgetReminderHook` and the `system_reminder` marker.

### Proposed Changes:

`SlidingWindowCompactor` builds the conversation it keeps out of historical turns and current-task Agent steps. A system reminder in the current task is part of neither, so every compaction removes it, even when only an old historical turn had to go. With the reminder hook registered before `CompactionHook`, this also removes the reminder added for the LLM call that is about to happen, so the model never sees "This is your last step":

```python
messages = [
    ChatMessage.from_system("You are helpful."),
    ChatMessage.from_user("old question"), ChatMessage.from_assistant("old answer " * 60),
    ChatMessage.from_user("current task"),
    *step(1), *step(2),  # tool call + tool result
    reminder,  # meta={"system_reminder": True}
]
SlidingWindowCompactor().compact(messages=messages, target_tokens=total - 50, token_counter=ApproximateTokenCounter())
# main:   system, "[3 earlier messages were removed ...]", task, step 1, step 2
# branch: system, "[2 earlier messages were removed ...]", task, step 1, step 2, reminder
```

`SummarizationCompactor` doesn't have this problem, because it only replaces the indices it selected.

With this change, a reminder in the current task goes with the Agent step that follows it, since that step is the model's response to it, so the two are kept or removed together. Reminders after the last step haven't been read yet: they are always kept and come off the budget with the other protected messages. The docs page for the sliding window and a release note are updated.

### How did you test it?

Two new tests in `test/hooks/compaction/test_sliding_window.py`, both failing on `main`:

- a reminder after the last step stays when only a historical turn is removed, and the note counts 2 removed messages, not 3
- a reminder between two steps stays with the newer step when the older one is removed

`hatch run test:unit` on Windows with Python 3.13: 7073 passed on this branch and 7071 on `main`, with the same single unrelated failure on both (`test_from_file_path_guess_mime_type[spam.csv]`, which depends on the Windows MIME registry). `hatch run test:types` is clean, and ruff check and format pass.

### Notes for the reviewer

#13375 changes the same function to keep summaries left by other compaction strategies. The two changes touch different lines, but whichever lands second will need a small rebase, which I'm happy to do.

title: fix: keep underscore-prefixed parameters in tool schemas
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13472 (https://github.com/deepset-ai/haystack/issues/13472)

### Proposed Changes:

`create_tool_from_function` and `@tool` built a Pydantic model with `(annotation, default)` fields. Pydantic treats a name that starts with `_` as a private attribute, so parameters such as `_tenant` never appeared in `model_json_schema()`. A required parameter was then impossible for the model to supply, and `Tool.invoke` failed with a missing argument. A defaulted parameter was dropped the same way.

`ComponentTool` hit the same Pydantic rule. It passed `Field(...)` under the real input name, so a component input such as `_tenant` raised `SchemaGenerationError` instead of being omitted. Dataclass fields used by parameter schemas did the same, except `ChatMessage`, which already strips the leading underscore so the schema matches `ChatMessage.from_dict`.

Underscore-prefixed names now get a safe internal field name and `Field(alias=param_name)`. `model_json_schema()` uses the alias, so the schema exposes `_tenant`, `required` stays correct, and defaults and descriptions are unchanged. Descriptions from `Annotated` metadata are still applied after schema generation. `tool.invoke(**args)` passes `_tenant=...` through to the function. `ChatMessage` schema keys are unchanged.

### How did you test it?

Reproduced with the script from the issue, on main, before the fix:

```
schema: {'properties': {'order_id': {'type': 'string'}}, 'required': ['order_id'], 'type': 'object'}
invoke FAILED: ToolInvocationError ... missing 1 required positional argument: '_tenant'
```

Added tests, then ran them against that same code. All six failed:

- `test_from_function_keeps_underscore_prefixed_parameters` — schema had only `order_id`
- `test_tool_decorator_keeps_underscore_prefixed_parameters` — same drop
- `test_from_function_underscore_parameter_does_not_replace_unprefixed_name` — `_tenant` missing beside `tenant`
- `test_component_tool_keeps_underscore_prefixed_inputs` — `SchemaGenerationError` / `Fields must not use names with leading underscores`
- `test_component_tool_keeps_underscore_dataclass_fields` — same Pydantic error while converting the dataclass
- `test_resolve_type_keeps_underscore_dataclass_fields` — same error

After the fix, those tests pass. They check that a required `_tenant` and a defaulted `_note` are in the schema, `required` lists only the required names, `Annotated` and docstring descriptions are kept, `jsonschema` rejects a payload that omits `_tenant`, `invoke(_tenant=..., order_id=...)` returns the function result, and `to_dict` / `from_dict` round-trips the schema.

The issue script now prints a schema with both `_tenant` and `order_id` required. Its `invoke(order_id="A-1")` call still fails, because that call leaves out the required `_tenant`. Calling with `_tenant` succeeds, which the tests cover.

Also ran:

- `hatch -e test run pytest -m "not integration" test/tools/test_from_function.py test/tools/test_component_tool.py test/tools/test_parameters_schema_utils.py test/tools/test_tool.py` — 140 passed, 2 skipped
- `hatch run fmt` / `hatch run fmt-check` — ruff clean
- `hatch run test:types` — mypy clean (566 files)
- `reno lint`

### Notes for the reviewer

The internal Pydantic name is not part of the schema. If the stripped name would collide with another parameter (`tenant` and `_tenant`) or is not a usable identifier (`_` or `_class`), the helper picks another internal name and still aliases the real one.

`ChatMessage` still drops the underscore on `_role`, `_content`, `_name`, and `_meta`. That path is separate from this alias fix and the existing schema tests still match.

title: fix: ImageFileToImageContent skips non-image files gracefully
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13446

### Proposed Changes:

ImageFileToImageContent now gracefully skips non-image files in batches instead of failing the entire batch.

**Problem**: When encountering a non-image file (e.g., a .txt file with MIME type text/plain) in a mixed batch:
1. The component caught encoding errors and skipped them
2. But ImageContent.__post_init__ validation happened **outside** the try-catch block
3. MIME type validation would raise ValueError: text/plain is not a valid image MIME type.
4. This crashed the entire run() call instead of skipping just that source

title: fix: keep literal NA and N/A cell values in XLSXToDocument #12945
body:
pandas.read_excel reads text such as "NA", "N/A", "NULL", "None", or "nan" as a missing value by default, so XLSXToDocument wrote those cells out as empty, the same as a truly empty cell.

title: fix: keep detected MIME type when FileTypeRouter attaches metadata
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13417

### Proposed Changes:

When `meta` is passed to `FileTypeRouter.run()`, a `Path` source is turned into a `ByteStream` with `get_bytestream_from_source()`. That utility defaults to `guess_mime_type=False`, so the resulting `ByteStream` had `mime_type=None` even though the router had already detected the MIME type and used it to pick the output bucket.

The detected MIME type is now carried onto the copy that receives the metadata:

```python
source = replace(source, meta={**source.meta, **meta_dict}, mime_type=source.mime_type or mime_type)
```

Effects:

- `router.run(sources=[path], meta={...})["text/plain"][0].mime_type` is now `"text/plain"` instead of `None`, matching the no-metadata path (which returns the original `Path`).
- `FileToFileContent` no longer logs `Failed to guess the MIME type of the file...` for sources routed with metadata.
- `ByteStream` inputs are unchanged: they keep the MIME type they were created with, and an unknown MIME type stays `None`.

### How did you test it?

```
$ pytest test/components/routers/test_file_router.py -q
36 passed
```

The new regression test `test_run_with_meta_keeps_detected_mime_type` fails without the change:

```
>       assert output[r"text/plain"][0].mime_type == "text/plain"
E       AssertionError: assert None == 'text/plain'
```

and passes with it. `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on both touched files.

### Notes for the reviewer

The fix only sets the MIME type when the converted stream does not already have one (`source.mime_type or mime_type`), so it cannot overwrite a MIME type a caller set on a `ByteStream` input.

title: fix: reject max_workers lower than 1 in parallel components
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13428

### Proposed Changes:

`MultiRetriever`, `MultiQueryTextRetriever`, `MultiQueryEmbeddingRetriever`, `LLMMetadataExtractor` and `LLMDocumentContentExtractor` now validate `max_workers` in `__init__` and raise

```
ValueError: `max_workers` must be at least 1, got 0.
```

This mirrors `OpenAIDecisionsDocumentClassifier`, which already follows this pattern.

Before this change the same configuration behaved differently depending on how the component was run:

- `run()` failed later, inside `concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor`, with `ValueError: max_workers must be greater than 0` raised at a line unrelated to where the invalid value was set.
- `run_async()` silently clamped the value with `max(1, self.max_workers)` and worked.

The failure is now raised where the mistake is made, and sync and async execution agree.

- Docstrings gained a `:raises ValueError:` entry for the new validation.
- Regression tests parametrized over `0` and `-1` for each of the five components.
- Release note added under `releasenotes/notes`.

The existing `max(1, ...)` clamps in the async paths are left untouched: they are now unreachable for values below 1, and keeping them avoids changing behaviour for any subclass that sets `self.max_workers` after construction.

### How did you test it?

Unit tests on the affected component suites:

```
$ pytest test/components/extractors test/components/retrievers -q -k "max_workers or init or to_dict or from_dict"
107 passed, 272 deselected
```

The new tests fail on `main` (10 failures, one per component and value) and pass with this change:

```
$ git checkout main -- haystack/components/retrievers haystack/components/extractors
$ pytest -q -k "invalid_max_workers" test/components/retrievers test/components/extractors
10 failed
```

`ruff check` and `ruff format --check` pass on every touched file.

### Notes for the reviewer

`MultiRetriever` already raised `ValueError` for non-positive `top_k`/`top_k_per_retriever` in `__init__`; `max_workers` was the only parallel knob left unvalidated.

title: fix: skip non-image sources in ImageFileToImageContent
body:
### Related Issues

- Fixes #13446

### Proposed Changes

`ImageFileToImageContent` used to build and validate `ImageContent` outside the `try` block that handles per-source conversion failures. A source that exists but is not an image (for example a `.txt` file in a mixed batch) therefore raised `ValueError: text/plain is not a valid image MIME type.` and discarded every source in the call.

This change moves the `ImageContent` construction into the existing `try`, so an invalid/non-image source is logged and skipped like an unreadable file, while valid sources are still returned.

### How did you test it?

Added a regression test that converts a valid JPEG and a text file together and asserts that only the image is returned with a `"Could not convert file"` warning. The test fails on `main` with the `ValueError` above and passes with the fix.

- `pytest -q test/components/converters/image/test_file_to_image.py` — 12 passed

title: fix!: move OpenAI chat generators to gpt-5.6-terra and keep tool calls working
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13438

### Proposed Changes:

OpenAI shuts down `gpt-5-mini`, the default model of `OpenAIChatGenerator` and `OpenAIResponsesChatGenerator`, on December 11, 2026 and names `gpt-5.6-terra` as the replacement ([deprecations](https://developers.openai.com/api/docs/deprecations)). Switching the name alone isn't enough: over Chat Completions, `gpt-5.6-terra` returns HTTP 400 for function tools unless `reasoning_effort` is `"none"`, and its default effort is `medium`. So an `Agent` on the default generator would fail.

- Change the default model of `OpenAIChatGenerator` and `OpenAIResponsesChatGenerator` to `gpt-5.6-terra`.
- In `OpenAIChatGenerator._prepare_api_call`: when the request includes tools, the model name starts with `gpt-5.6`, `gpt-6-sol`, or `gpt-6-luna`, and `reasoning_effort` isn't set, send `reasoning_effort="none"`. OpenAI's model pages for gpt-6-sol and gpt-6-luna say "Chat Completions supports function calling only with `reasoning_effort` set to `none`". The rule only changes requests that OpenAI would otherwise reject. An explicit `reasoning_effort` is left alone, and `self.generation_kwargs` isn't mutated.
- Document `reasoning_effort` in the `generation_kwargs` docstring and on the OpenAIChatGenerator docs page, and point to `OpenAIResponsesChatGenerator` for reasoning with tools.
- Update every doc page that names the default model
- Replace explicit `gpt-5-mini` in docs examples:
  - The token budget and Tavily Agent examples now use `OpenAIChatGenerator()` instead of restating a model.
  - The `OpenAITokenCounter` and `StreamingChunk` examples name `gpt-5.6-terra`.
- Lower the token budget example's threshold from 3,000 to 100 tokens, in the basic and `add_final_message` snippets:
  - `gpt-5.6-terra` makes all its searches in the first LLM call and answers in the second. The hook checks the budget only before the second call, when usage is about 250 tokens, so a budget of 3,000 never triggered and the example printed `text` instead of the documented `token_budget_exceeded`.
  - The first call's prompt alone is 159 tokens, so a budget of 100 always stops the run before the answer.

### How did you test it?

- New unit tests: `reasoning_effort="none"` is sent for gpt-5.6 and gpt-6-sol with tools; an explicit `reasoning_effort` is kept; it isn't sent for `gpt-5.4` (whose default is already `none`) or when there are no tools.
- Probed Chat Completions directly with one function tool, sending no `reasoning_effort`, then `"none"`, then `"low"`:

  | Model | No effort | `"none"` | `"low"` |
  | --- | --- | --- | --- |
  | `gpt-5.6-terra`, `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-6-sol`, `gpt-6-luna` | 400 | tool call | 400 |
  | `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-6.1-sol` | 400 | 400 (`none` unsupported) | 400 |
  | `gpt-5.4` | tool call | tool call | 400 |
  | `gpt-5-mini` | tool call | 400 (`none` unsupported) | tool call |

  This matches the prefix list. `gpt-5.4` has the same restriction but defaults to `none`, so it needs nothing.
- Live tests on a local merge with #13441: all relevant integration tests pass
- Ran the updated examples except for the tavily example

### Notes for the reviewer

- Overlaps with #13441. I'll rebase once #13441 is merged.
- Azure: `AzureOpenAIChatGenerator` inherits the rule, so a deployment named `gpt-5.6-*` gets it too. I left the default deployment name of `AzureOpenAIResponsesChatGenerator` (`gpt-5-mini`) unchanged because Azure has its own retirement schedule.

title: feat: add per-query missing-document diagnostics to DocumentRecallEvaluator
body:
### Related Issues

- addresses #13418

### Proposed Changes:

Add an opt-in `include_diagnostics` parameter to `DocumentRecallEvaluator`. With
`include_diagnostics=True`, `run()` returns three additional outputs alongside the
unchanged `score` and `individual_scores`:

- `missing_documents`: for each query, the comparison values (as configured by
  `document_comparison_field`) of the ground truth documents that were not retrieved,
  deduplicated and in ground truth order.
- `support_coverage`: for each query, the fraction of ground truth documents retrieved.
  This is reported independently of the recall mode, so in `single_hit` mode it exposes
  partial coverage that the 0/1 individual score hides.
- `all_support_rate`: the fraction of queries for which every ground truth document
  was retrieved.

The default (`include_diagnostics=False`) preserves the existing outputs, scoring
semantics, and serialized form for existing pipelines; diagnostics were verified
end-to-end in a `Pipeline`, including a serialization round trip.

### How did you test it?

Added 11 unit tests in `test/components/evaluators/test_document_recall.py`
(`TestDocumentRecallEvaluatorDiagnostics`) covering the diagnostics outputs in both
recall modes, the configured comparison fields (`content`, `id`), deduplication and
ordering of missing documents, empty ground truth / retrieved inputs, and
serialization with and without the new parameter. Full file: 56 passed; the whole
`test/components/evaluators/` suite passes (203 passed, 4 skipped).

### Notes for the reviewer

- The issue proposes this as an optional extension of the existing evaluator rather
  than a separate component, which is the approach taken here; the output names and
  the `include_diagnostics` flag are easy to adjust if you prefer a different shape.
- Happy to add a docs example if you would like one.

title: fix: report per-piece line ranges for PythonCodeSplitter secondary splits
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13436

### Proposed Changes:

When an oversized function or method goes through the line-based secondary split, every piece got a deep copy of the whole unit's metadata, including `start_line` / `end_line`. So all pieces of one function pointed at the same full range.

`_secondary_split` now maps each piece back to the file lines it covers, using the `split_idx_start` offset `DocumentSplitter` already sets. The unit source ends at `unit.end_line` and may begin a few lines earlier (blank lines and comments before the `def`), so the first physical line is `end_line - line_count(source) + 1`. Each piece's range is clamped to the function's `start_line`..`end_line`, which matches how primary chunks treat leading blank lines and comments. Lines are counted with `io.StringIO(newline="")`, the same `\n` / `\r\n` / `\r` rule `_extract_units` uses after #13301.

When `strip_docstrings=True` removed a docstring, the unit source no longer lines up with the file, so those pieces keep the function's full range as before.

### How did you test it?

- New test `test_secondary_split_pieces_report_their_own_line_range`: checks that each piece's `start_line..end_line` slice of the source matches the piece content, and that the ranges are increasing and span the function. It fails on main and passes with the fix.
- `pytest test/components/preprocessors/test_python_code_splitter.py`: 75 passed.
- `ruff check` / `ruff format --check` clean.

### Notes for the reviewer

Other metadata (`unit_kinds`, `qualified_name`, `secondary_split_index`, ...) is unchanged. Only the line range is narrowed per piece. The class docstring mentions this.

title: fix: match the LinkContentFetcher content type case-insensitively
body:
### Related Issues

- No existing issue. I searched open and closed issues and PRs for `LinkContentFetcher` content type handling and didn't find this one.

### Proposed Changes:

`LinkContentFetcher._get_content_type` returns the `Content-Type` header value as sent by the server, only cutting off the parameters. Media types are case-insensitive (RFC 9110, section 8.3.1), but the handler lookup is not: the direct lookup in `self.handlers` is an exact dict match, and `fnmatch` is case-sensitive on Linux and macOS (it only normalizes case on Windows).

So a response with `Content-Type: Application/PDF` or `IMAGE/PNG` doesn't match `application/*` or `image/*` and falls back to the text handler. That handler returns `response.text`, i.e. the binary body decoded as text and re-encoded as UTF-8, so the returned `ByteStream` holds a corrupted file. The non-normalized value is also stored as `meta["content_type"]` and `mime_type`, which then doesn't match routers such as `FileTypeRouter`.

Reproduction on `main`:

```python
import httpx
from haystack.components.fetchers import LinkContentFetcher

pdf = b"%PDF-1.4\n\xe2\xe3\xcf\xd3\n"
transport = httpx.MockTransport(lambda request: httpx.Response(200, headers={"Content-Type": "Application/PDF"}, content=pdf))
stream = LinkContentFetcher(client_kwargs={"transport": transport}).run(urls=["https://example.com/doc"])["streams"][0]
print(stream.mime_type, stream.data == pdf)  # Application/PDF False
```

The fix lowercases the media type and strips surrounding whitespace in `_get_content_type`, which is used by both `run` and `run_async`.

### How did you test it?

- Added `test_run_binary_content_type_is_case_insensitive` (sync, parametrized with mixed case, parameters and extra whitespace) and `test_run_async_binary_content_type_is_case_insensitive`. They fail on `main` and pass with the fix.
- `pytest test/components/fetchers/test_link_content_fetcher.py -m "not integration"`: 34 passed.
- `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` on the changed files.

### Notes for the reviewer

The stored `content_type` is now always lowercase. For servers that already send lowercase types nothing changes.

### Related Issues

- fixes #13428


### Proposed Changes

`MultiRetriever`, `MultiQueryTextRetriever`, `MultiQueryEmbeddingRetriever`, `LLMMetadataExtractor `and `LLMDocumentContentExtractor `accepted` max_workers < 1` without validation. The bad value only surfaced later and inconsistently:` run() `failed inside `ThreadPoolExecutor ``(ValueError: max_workers must be greater than 0`), while` run_async()` silently clamped it to 1 via `Semaphore(max(1, self.max_workers)).`

- removes the now-unneeded` max(1, ...)` clamp in each `run_async`, so sync and async behave the same;

- documents the new `ValueError `in the docstrings.

Since from_dict goes through `__init__`, invalid serialized pipelines are rejected at load time too.

title: fix: align rows by an input column and keep same-named runs in comparative_detailed_report
body:
### Related Issues

- fixes #13425

### Proposed Changes:

`comparative_detailed_report` paired the two runs' rows by position. If the second run evaluated the same questions in a different order, or not all of the same ones, its scores ended up next to the wrong questions without any error. Runs with the same `run_name` also overwrote each other's columns.

Some history: when the comparison was added in #7594, it warned if the runs' input values differed and renamed same-named runs to `_first`/`_second`. #7603 reduced the check to column names (likely because inputs like `predicted_answer` always differ between runs), and #8838 dropped the `_first`/`_second` names when the method stopped using pandas.

Changes:
- New keyword-only `align_on` parameter to match rows by an input column, like a question ID or the question itself. Strings are matched with whitespace collapsed but case kept, since IDs can be case-sensitive. Repeated values are paired in order. Rows without a match are kept with `None` for the other run (rows only in `other` are added at the end), with a warning.
- Without `align_on`, rows are still matched by position, but a warning suggests `align_on` when the runs have a different number of rows, or a value that appears once in each run sits in a different row. Repeated values (like "I don't know" answers) are ignored for this check, and columns that can't be hashed, like Documents, are skipped.
- Same-named runs get `_first`/`_second` column names again.

When the runs already line up, the report is exactly the same as before.

### How did you test it?

- Added tests for reordered rows, rows missing in either run, repeated values, whitespace vs case, a missing `align_on` column, `keep_columns` staying with their rows, same run names, the misalignment warning, and no warning for aligned runs or unhashable columns. 10 of them fail on main.
- Ran the evaluation and evaluator unit tests, plus `fmt-check` and `types` on the changed files.
- Checked a realistic case (an HR test set where the second run is reordered, drops one question, adds one, has a double space and a repeated question): with `align_on="query_id"` every row matches the right scores.

### Notes for the reviewer

- Without `align_on`, runs with a different number of rows now get `None`-padded rows instead of columns of different lengths.
- The misalignment warning can rarely fire on aligned runs if an identical answer happens to appear once in each run for different questions. Since we can't know which column identifies the rows without `align_on`, the warning doesn't suggest a specific column.
- Values that differ only in capitalization aren't matched by `align_on`. They show up as unmatched rows with a warning.

title: fix: preserve PythonCodeSplitter member decorator boundaries
body:
### Related Issues

No matching bug report found. The original Python splitter feature is #11354. This is separate from the docstring stripping fix in #13309 and qualified-name metadata work in #11875.

### Proposed Changes:

`PythonCodeSplitter(preserve_class_definition=True)` currently includes the first class member's decorators in the reusable class signature. This duplicates them on that member and copies them onto unrelated later members. For example, a first `@property` makes the chunk for a later ordinary method look like another property.

Use the first decorator marker as the member boundary. AST expression line numbers alone are insufficient for parenthesized multiline decorators: the expression can begin after the `@(` line. A single lexical pass maps decorator-expression lines to their opening marker; the same boundary helper is used for class signatures, class headers, members and top-level definitions. Only a logical line's first meaningful `@` counts, not matrix multiplication. Newlines are normalized for lexing only; output slices retain original source spelling.

This also keeps parenthesized decorators with their definitions and reports their actual marker in `start_line`. Ordinary decorator and undecorated metadata is unchanged. This does not redesign the existing bare class-header chunk or promise independently executable chunks.

### How did you test it?

All project execution used Hatch, with Python 3.12.14 and a reduced local test environment (not included in this PR).

- Full `test/components/preprocessors/test_python_code_splitter.py`: 134 passed, one existing Document-mutation warning; independently rerun with the same result.
- The 60 added parametrized cases on pristine base `76fc2d3d7492ec243eed40eb939a836f2a8b29da`: 46 failed, 14 passed. They cover first methods, async methods, nested classes, outer classes, top-level functions, parenthesized decorators, comments, preservation on/off, LF/CRLF/CR, exact ordered content and source metadata.
- Independent supplemental checks: 756 cases passed (144 intended differences and 612 identical controls), plus 450 lexical-boundary cases passed. Extraction compatibility across 295 package Python files found no new errors or changes to unit contents and ordinary metadata; the intentionally changed `class_signature` field was excluded from that compatibility comparison.
- Targeted Ruff check and format check, targeted mypy with `--follow-imports=silent`, release-note backtick check, and `git diff --check` passed.
- Not run: full pre-commit aggregate (including codespell), full repository tests/type aggregate, network/model integrations, or multiple Python versions. Targeted checks are not a claim that full pre-commit passed.

### Notes for the reviewer

This implementation, tests and PR description were generated by AI assistants. A separate AI reviewer reviewed the revised patch and independently reran the checks described above. The account owner has reviewed and understood the changes. Tests were executed by the preparing AI assistant and independent AI reviewer.

The additional token pass has a measurable cost. Five-run median extraction-only measurements for 1,000 synthetic definitions were 9.52 ms → 17.06 ms for plain functions and 13.24 ms → 24.50 ms for decorated functions, approximately 1.8x at that stage. These are not end-to-end throughput measurements. The implementation tokenizes once per input, not once per definition.

- Closes #13420 

### Proposed Changes

`MetadataRouter.from_dict()` previously deserialized `output_type` directly inside the dictionary supplied by the caller. This replaced the serialized type string with a live Python type and caused a second deserialization of the same configuration to fail.

title: fix: reject non-star string extra_meta_fields in JSONConverter
body:
### Related Issues

- Companion hardening to #13070 (same unvalidated-`Literal` family; this PR covers `JSONConverter`, a component that issue does not touch).

### Proposed Changes:

`JSONConverter.__init__` accepted any value for `extra_meta_fields` (annotated `set[str] | Literal["*"] | None`). Because `run()` only special-cases the exact string `"*"` and otherwise iterates the value (`for field in meta_fields:`), a plain string typo was silently iterated **character by character**:

```python
converter = JSONConverter(content_key="title", extra_meta_fields="author")
converter.run(sources=[ByteStream(b'{"title": "Dune", "author": "Frank Herbert"}')])
# documents[0].meta == {'a': None, 'u': None, 't': None, 'h': None, 'o': None, 'r': None}
```

The intended field is dropped and six meaningless keys flow into the indexing pipeline unnoticed. A near-miss of the literal (`"**"`) produces `{'*': None}` the same way, and since the value is part of the serialized config, a YAML round-trip can inject it without a type checker ever seeing it.

This PR validates in `__init__`: a string other than the literal `'*'` now raises immediately with an actionable message, mirroring the constructor validation `XLSXToDocument` already performs for its own `Literal` parameters. `None`, `'*'`, sets, and the list form accepted by `Pipeline` deserialization are unaffected.

### How did you test it?

- New unit tests: `test_init_rejects_non_star_string_extra_meta_fields` (asserts the `ValueError` for `"author"` and `"**"`) and `test_init_accepts_star_literal_extra_meta_fields` (asserts `'*'` still constructs).
- Before the change, the reproducer above yields the per-character metadata; after it, construction fails fast.
- Full `test/components/converters/test_json.py` suite passes (32 tests), `ruff check` and `ruff format --check` clean.

### Notes for the reviewer

- The validation intentionally runs before the `jq` import check so a misconfigured component fails on the configuration error, not on an unrelated dependency message.
- Deliberately out of scope: coercing `list`/`tuple` inputs to `set` — the list form is accepted by existing `from_dict` tests and behaves correctly when iterated; only the string case silently corrupts metadata.
